tu.686fba6939a6d2622c0d91cf:
You step closer. The table and the book are covered in thick dust. A shiver runs down your spine at the thought of how long no one has been here. Why would anyone leave a book in a forgotten, godforsaken dungeon? Were they hiding it?
You pick up the book. Though it has sat here for ages, it feels untouched by time. You brush your hand over the cover, wiping away dust, but there is no title. Curious.
You tuck the book into your bag. Maybe at your next rest you can read it.
tu.686fbb319c3720ef9d0aef02: Now it feels like there’s nothing left to do in the ruins. It’s time to continue.
tu.686fc37c531801da263a55fd: Targrad won’t wait! It's best to return to the road.
tu.686fc4c983397c79622dd2e1: There was a battlefield nearby. It's worth investigating it in daylight.
tu.686fcc25079e4122916549da: Perhaps it's best to stay up here. You don’t want to break your legs.
tu.686fcc2e3d1e50d238da085f: You decide not to take the risk. It’s clearly just a regular basement in front of you. What could you possibly find down there, a sack of rotten old potatoes? A pack of starving rats? Definitely not worth it. You turn away, adjust the bag on your shoulder, and start thinking about what to do next.
tu.686fd0bf826f810da14b4971: There was a battlefield nearby. It's worth investigating it and praying for the souls of the fallen.
tu.686fd456363c1bebe55e5e7e: There was a battlefield nearby. It's worth investigating it and praying for the unresting souls.
tu.687133cc21f429ac729bf514:
You don’t want to waste your precious time. The sun rises higher and higher. If you hurry, you’ll reach Targrad before sunset.
You gather your belongings, packing everything into your simple backpack. The road doesn’t wait.
tu.6871343aaef29a5a4673a19f: It’s worth examining everything more closely.
tu.68713538d7a7c844e865cd98: Yes, it’s time to head to Targrad. Someone is waiting for you there.
tu.6871353e7dde35cb6f544c84: You pack your few belongings into a canvas bag. A light breeze ruffles your hair. The day promises to be excellent. You are ready to move forward.
tu.687135ff6fb1e1f58079646f: It’s disgusting here. Not worth wasting time. Someone is waiting for you in Targrad.
tu.687138d1d2869c07581dea85: No, nothing will. Not worth wasting time. Time to head to Targrad.
tu.68713cb61fcd5968859b9ad2: Perhaps it’s worth checking something not too high up. You won’t have to climb if you notice something interesting.
tu.6873ca374fdfa8fc0a7df14b: Climb straight along the wall. It looks solid enough, and the broken sections even resemble steps somewhat. What could go wrong?
tu.6873ca4007991b6a0419e53c: You’ll have to climb high, but you’re confident you can manage it. You place your foot, grip with your hands, and pull yourself up. The brickwork is barely visible beneath last year’s leaves and other debris. You need to focus as you make your way upward.
tu.6873ca4ec69b0b7608b2f62f: You climb higher and higher. Disturbed birds take off, squawking in protest at your intrusion. You smile. There’s a light breeze here that doesn’t reach the ground. You think you worried for nothing—this is much easier than it looked.
tu.6873ca54281119b5cefb6631:
Now you’re almost at the nest. You tilt your head and realize that a second floor or balcony once began here. The walls are gone now, so from this height you get a stunning view of the surroundings.
You exhale in delight. The wind brushes your cheeks, and birds sing around you. What could be more like paradise?
You take a step forward, but the brick under your foot crumbles unexpectedly. You lose your balance.
tu.6873ca6e71c782cfc8eaa261: Crouch down as quickly as possible to regain balance!
tu.6873ca7a431e94fabf3a3b59: You try, really, but the bricks, long destroyed inside by time, crack and crumble beneath your feet. No matter what you do, how you move or wave your arms, you topple to the side.
tu.6873ca8ac004a4f9613bada0:
You fall. You gasp for air in a vain attempt to save yourself. Your primal instinct screams that this is the end; your mind tells you nothing terrible will happen. But you can’t see that you’re falling straight onto a sharp broken stone.
A second later, your spine snaps with a deafening crack. The stone breaks something. Something very important.
tu.6873ca9d34b007b9d13a9e13: You try to move your arms and legs, but nothing responds. You hope it’s temporary, but neither after five minutes nor an hour does it get any better. You don’t feel your body, you can only move your head and eyes.
tu.6873caa118f31dfe1131af58: You try to cry out, but barely manage a breath. Panic washes over you. You can’t feel your hands or legs. Birds perch on the fallen wall, looking at you as if mocking.
tu.6873caaceeee3ab0e5af7153:
You realize that no one will find you, no one will save you. Birds will peck your eyes, wild animals will gnaw your bones. You will remain here as the silent guardian of the abandoned temple.
Your story ends here.
tu.6873cba911d8e0bab641c7cf: The ladder was so close! But you don’t want to tear your clothes. You’ll climb up without it.
tu.6873cbb0dc64fc0bbdddb5bd: You return to the wall, humbled by the rose bushes but intact. You don’t have a change of clothes with you, and you don’t want to appear before the ruler of Targrad looking like a commoner.
tu.6873cc38859a54ee28410ff3: Can’t go on! Screw this ladder!
tu.6873cc3cc7e81845d6bf6c24:
You give up. You’re defeated. The rose bushes have done their job guarding the ladder perfectly.
You step back, freeing yourself from the thorns, quietly cursing. There’s only one way left to climb.
tu.6873e7e3c444bcfe4a679ffd:
You approach again. Over the years without people here, grass has grown through the stone floor slabs, now reaching almost to your knees. Moss and ivy cover the walls. Everywhere you feel nature reclaiming what once belonged to it.
You push aside the flexible ivy stems and tug the handle. The door won’t budge.
tu.6873e7fc5a9df7e7b14f5ef8: Seems like it needs a key.
tu.6873e8072db294fd24c4b44c: You tug the handle again. The door still won’t budge. Who even thought of locking something in a ruined temple?! It seems you really do need to find a key. But where could it be?
tu.6873e80cd1d12a4f5486c8d6: You decide not to waste your strength on a pointless effort. There’s a keyhole under the handle, so you need to find a key. But where could it be?
tu.6873e84e40f11322c8525537: It’s worth looking around again. You think you saw something... Yes, up there!
tu.6873e85044d15b6df15956cf: Need to look around more carefully.
tu.6873e8d6d3bec3ad819a492a: You look up again. There, in the nest, you spotted a glint. Surely a curious bird dragged a key up there! You need to climb and check.
tu.6873e8dc670c7235bca65079: You look around, raising your gaze. On the broken walls are ivy, small flowers, bird nests. You notice a glint in one of them. Perhaps a bird stole a shiny object, or maybe an entire key! You need to get up there and check.
tu.6873e9d099317b3cecd6600f: It's worth checking the roof. Maybe there’s something interesting there.
tu.6873ef686d39519967e28201:
No, your curiosity won’t be tamed so easily. Inside you itch to open the door and see what’s behind it. Could there be treasures? Or secret records of monks who once lived here?
You just don’t want to think you might find an ordinary broom closet.
tu.6873f0c1ef7d4f1799e5bbc8: Need to pray for the dead.
tu.6873f0c55fc6f581666eb2bf: It's worth returning to the temple ruins.
tu.6873f12ef6c147ad578d426c: It's a dead horse... It's worth examining it closer.
tu.6873f1438ad3b789e521fc7d: You approach the bodies lying on the ground. A light breeze blows, letting you inhale without the stench of decay. Now you can examine the bodies and pray for those who have departed this world.
tu.6873f151a8afba53324857d5: Examine the bodies more closely first.
tu.6873f1618986e8843a346867:
You fold your hands in a prayer gesture and begin to recite the words silently. Around you, there are so many sounds, but you focus only on the sacred words. You even feel as if you’re back in a temple in your hometown. You sincerely hope that all these fallen warriors find peace.
Finally, the prayer comes to an end. You open your eyes and immediately notice a strange ring on one of the dead men.
tu.6873f16fdc97cb525c02bf8b:
You move closer. It hasn’t rained in a long time, so the ground is dry and dusty. Next to the bodies, the grass is stained with dried blood. Even in this proximity, the wind doesn’t mask the scent.
Your gaze slides over the fallen.
tu.6873f1807be2937ac8cf86bd: Saddening. They still had life ahead of them.
tu.6873f18a323165df573a3bd6:
You shake your head, looking at the bodies with sorrow. War spares no one, neither the young nor the old.
Suddenly, your attention is drawn to the ring on one of the dead men.
tu.6873f1933d8eee9ece7cb86d:
You purse your lips, looking at the bodies. You feel no pity: these people chose this path. Any warrior risks ending up a corpse among crows.
Your eyes sweep over the fallen, and you notice the glint of a ring on one of them.
tu.6873f19d19515264a10cebb6: You move closer. The corpse lies in an unnatural position, but his eyes are closed and his face is peaceful. You immediately notice that the man’s clothing is richer than the others’. Interesting. What's his story? And that ring... It draws your gaze.
tu.6873f1c51b6b41b0700fe7c1: Leave the ring with the dead man.
tu.6873f1d06d52581950bc9266: You look around, as if someone might see you. You’ve never stolen anything, but... the owner of the ring is already dead, he doesn’t need it anymore. By taking it, you give it a second life, preventing it from staying buried. You soothe yourself with this thought as you remove the ring from the lifeless hand. It feels as if the corpse might squeeze his hand and growl, but nothing happens. You simply take the ring and place it in your bag.
tu.6873f1d64051ab8d22b0c5f6:
No, you can’t do that. You’re not a thief! The ring belonged to this man in life, so it belongs to him in death.
You step back, feeling a strange relief, as if you’ve just resisted a terrible temptation.
tu.6873f2210d3bb698ed24abdd: You cast one last glance at the fallen warriors. What to do now?
tu.6873f280f715648e6e64c260: The temple ruins might hide something interesting.
tu.6873f299d50e02b8325f35ad: You return to the temple where you spent the night. You still have a little time to explore it.
tu.68741733567677e39341276d: You approach the horse. The smell is suffocating and sharp, making your eyes water. You look at the poor animal and the broken cart nearby. War shows no mercy to anyone, not even animals.
tu.68741773cf32f4e4ac6dcbaa:
It seems you know everything about this conflict. Two families are fighting each other, secretly supported by far more powerful forces. Your Order chose a policy of non-interference. At least, that’s what you’re all supposed to say. In reality... you haven’t climbed high enough yet to see the full picture. But perhaps after delivering this message, you’ll finally be accepted into the inner circle.
You can’t resist imagining what you would do if you had access to such power.
tu.68741792408c6dd58a32aaac:
You think it’s terribly unfair. Surely most of those lying on the dry ground before you saw something greater in the war. Perhaps they fought for an ideal. You dislike this. If you had power, you would do everything possible to free this world from war.
Everything possible.
tu.687417997def4b3a04337fb7: In this world, someone is always fighting someone else. It’s an endless cycle that people like your Order have learned to exploit. And you understand it. Eternal wars — this is what allows you to exist, what sustains your prosperity. So let them fight, let them die for the sake of a greater idea.
tu.687417a9bb9fcf744631f4c3:
You cast your gaze into the distance and smile faintly. Tonight, you will have completed everything required of you. In a few days, you’ll return to the Order. You’re confident the elders will reward you.
But for now, you need to focus on your task.
tu.687417d37546a6e953a425dc: Examine the bodies of the warriors before hitting the road.
tu.687418b1cf45f50f3dee055f: Take one last look at the temple ruins.
tu.68741ca36c269d09a0c48504: Time to set out for Targrad.
tu.68741d0bd37cc2c886d55c12: You leave the battlefield. With each step, the smell grows weaker until it disappears entirely near the temple ruins.
tu.6874352c8e9be35fe2e6a4e4: You glance back at the abandoned temple. For some reason, you have the feeling you’re seeing it for the last time. Shaking off the thought, you return to the road.
tu.68743a8be214531c35abd350: You’ve already wasted a lot of precious time. Targrad doesn’t wait. You cast a short glance at the temple ruins and turn away. Pushing through the mixed grasses, you reach the road to Targrad. Tonight, you’ll sleep there in a real bed. The thought drives you forward.
tu.68743af2657d1731cc505626: The weather is beautiful, with a gentle breeze. You walk briskly. Targrad is close, though its towers are still hidden beyond the horizon.
tu.68743af43b46c3b5da7a9ec9: The weather is lovely, but walking is hard. Your scratches ache, but overall, you manage. By evening, it should feel better. Perhaps you’ll stay in Targrad a couple of days to recover.
tu.68743c2c3cf858c654c1368b: After a few hours of unhurried walking, you see the first modest houses. Your route passes through a tiny village. Once it thrived from trade coming from Targrad, but the war changed everything. Now there are fewer traders, less money. People are leaving. The road to Targrad isn’t long, but maybe it’s worth at least replenishing your water supplies?
tu.687edd1861c646039996ced7: Climb straight along the wall. It looks solid enough, and the broken sections even resemble steps somewhat. What could go wrong?
tu.6890fe835119dc389c315b2a:
You look closer. The temple’s skeleton rises from the forest like rotten teeth in a beauty’s mouth. You realize the place must have been huge. Perhaps a monastery once stood here, not just a church?..
Your gaze is drawn to a door almost completely hidden by greenery.

ru.682f27b9406ea97be6360e5d: Ты не сможешь сбежать из Таркова.
ru.682f27b95382320ebd9fd358: Ты ничего не понял. Это нормально.
ru.682f27b95608ddc120ab76cc: Для выживающего — да. Для того, кто обеспечивает выживаемость, всё иначе.
ru.682f27b9711105d12215b09a: Ты сам искал встречи со мной? Ты задавал вопрос себе — зачем?
ru.682f27b97b858b2564865937: Нам пока больше не о чем говорить. Ты сам всё поймёшь со временем, распутывая этот клубок.
ru.682f27b97f225b1bc52abbf4: Этому миру конец, все эти жалкие попытки удержаться на тающей льдине в центре бушующего океана - все эти локальные стычки, лицемерие торговцев, подстрекательство, насилие, помноженное на насилие.
ru.682f27b9979991b2e826a12b: Я не знаю... Я думал, что знакомство с таким человеком может мне что-то дать.
ru.682f27b99b07ec6d169a6d23: Да. Возможности менять окружение и как следствие — реальность.
ru.682f27b9b7f0d690dd0c67d8: Перерождение? Закат? О чём ты вообще?
ru.682f27b9c1ec27cb4cde39d6: Я - Смотритель. Смотрю за всем и за всеми, и все видят мой свет.
ru.682f27b9e09da7c498b55531: Приближенность к тому, для кого коллапс есть начало нового.
ru.68495cbd0da5f730bfb9bec0: В наше неспокойное время самое главное — обладать нужной информацией.
ru.68495cfcbbbd4a4cc1a4769a: Информация порождает связи, связи дают возможности.
ru.68495db939fef1a4a2a29362: В среде подобного рода базовая потребность человека — это выживание.
ru.68495de28c95841704ce1182: Я не хочу просто выживать, я хочу контролировать выживание.
ru.68495e691f7b8a8809240a91: Мы встретились неспроста. Во всех событиях есть смысл, случайностей не бывает.
ru.68495eeac180d86a1e8de129: Ты хочешь не просто выжить, ты хочешь контролировать ситуацию.
ru.68495faa9eea93de67288561: Всё это ведет к очень конкретному результату. Заката не будет, будет перерождение.
ru.68495fe15cd2fbaf2e85b196: Я тоже сначала ничего не понял, когда они связались со мной.
ru.684ac10d7a0624811d0ec52a: Кто я - в данный момент совсем не важно.
ru.684ac11bc7d26def739371c0: Важно, кто ты и зачем ты здесь.

sk.682f27b91331a31af346939b: Well, I'm going to try. And I was hoping you would help me with this.
sk.682f27b92a6337d2463e414c: So why do you need me?
sk.682f27b93267003f9caabe47: I want to escape from Tarkov.
sk.682f27b936657af3f59606d8: Tarkov is who you are. You cannot escape from yourself. Just as I could not escape from myself.
sk.682f27b9406ea97be6360e5d: You will not escape from Tarkov.
sk.682f27b95382320ebd9fd358: You don’t understand, but this is natural.
sk.682f27b95608ddc120ab76cc: It does, for the survivor. For someone who ensures survival, everything is different.
sk.682f27b966e6a42b0cf9299d: They? Who are you talking about?
sk.682f27b9711105d12215b09a: But it was you who was looking for me, wasn’t it? Did you ask yourself why?
sk.682f27b97b858b2564865937: There's nothing more for us to talk about. In time, you'll figure it out for yourself, as you unravel the tangle.
sk.682f27b97f225b1bc52abbf4: This world is ending, all these pathetic attempts to hold on to a melting ice floe in the middle of a raging ocean - all these local fights, the hypocrisy of the traders, the instigation, violence multiplied by violence.
sk.682f27b9979991b2e826a12b: I don't know... I thought knowing someone like you could give me something.
sk.682f27b99b07ec6d169a6d23: Yes. The opportunity to change the surroundings and, as a consequence, the reality.
sk.682f27b9b7f0d690dd0c67d8: Rebirth? Eclipse? The hell are you talking about?
sk.682f27b9c1ec27cb4cde39d6: I am Lightkeeper. I watch over everything and everyone, and all can see my light.
sk.682f27b9e09da7c498b55531: Being close to the one for whom the collapse is the beginning of the new.
sk.68495cbd0da5f730bfb9bec0: In our restless time, it's critical to have the necessary information.
sk.68495cfcbbbd4a4cc1a4769a: Information creates connections, connections yield opportunities.
sk.68495db939fef1a4a2a29362: In this kind of environment, the basic necessity for human beings is survival.
sk.68495de28c95841704ce1182: I don't want to simply survive, I want to control the survival.
sk.68495e691f7b8a8809240a91: We met for a reason. All events have a meaning, there are no accidents.
sk.68495eeac180d86a1e8de129: You don’t want to simply survive, you want to be in control.
sk.68495faa9eea93de67288561: All this leads to a very specific result. There will be no eclipse, there will be rebirth.
sk.68495fe15cd2fbaf2e85b196: I didn't understand it at first either, when they reached out to me.
sk.684ac10d7a0624811d0ec52a: Who I am is not important at all at the moment.
sk.684ac11bc7d26def739371c0: What matters is who you are and why you are here.

ch.68743d0df285ae400d661914:
After a few hours of unhurried walking, you see the first modest houses.

Your route passes through a tiny village. Once it thrived from trade coming from Targrad, but the war changed everything. Now there are fewer traders, less money. People are leaving. The road to Targrad isn’t long, but maybe it’s worth at least replenishing your water supplies?
ch.68743d72e63583c86c178242: Yes, it's best to stay here for a bit.
ch.68743d766f1e35975767990e: No, you have everything you need. Better hurry.
ch.68743d7bcb8ce2f65f19987e: You realize you have not eaten in a long time. And your water ran out last night. There is nowhere to resupply between here and Targrad, so it makes sense to stop.
ch.68743d808cc2bdc17eb7d442: You are not going to waste time. You have enough water, and you can grab a bite once you reach Targrad. The message is more important right now.
ch.68743d83ef859469e1da95d7: A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with chunks of meat. Both are working hard to draw you to their goods.
ch.68743d89f31067886c0f6235:
You walk straight through the village, not stopping anywhere. Today looks like market day: various goods are laid throughout the village's center. The locals watch you with a hint of hope, wishing you would buy something. You just keep walking.
At last, an outpost with a bridge over the river appears ahead. But something is off. No Targrad pennants, no guards... You stop just in time to notice men at the gate. Their armor is battered, their looks unkempt. They are definitely not soldiers. Goosebumps run down your back.
ch.68743dbb7c48f120d1b53172: You should probably go back to the village and ask the locals who they are and where the garrison went.
ch.68743dc0a13b10e7875570b0:
You retreat as quickly as you can. The men do not notice you. You have no idea what they are doing there, where the Targrad guards went, or how you are supposed to cross now...
You return to the village and look around. A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with a tray full of various sausages and pieces of dried meat. Both are trying hard to lure you to their goods.
ch.68743dff32194b7a514624e5:
The men spot you quickly, perk up, and shout,
— Hey you, what are you doing here? C'mere!
You come closer.
The men are armed and look hostile.
— So why're you here? Cat got your tongue? We can help you pull it out!
ch.68743e03f6173c9e91a166a0: You don't want to fight. Answer calmly.
ch.68743e07116888f39aef1d7e: Who do they think they are? You have a permit from the head of the Order to pass through all these lands!
ch.68743e231723328dcfa13297:
You lift your chin and walk straight toward the men. They notice you, exchange looks, and frown.
— So, why are you here? Need to get to the other side?
You nod.
— Then pay.
They smirk. One of them holds out his hand. You realize your travel charter signed by the head of the Order will not help here.
ch.68743e259520db6ad8760da8: Whoever they are, you need to get to the other side of the river. You will go to them by yourself.
ch.68743e337348f6ea87d4816f:
— I need to get to the other side.
Yes, a very diplomatic answer!
— Then pay.
ch.68743e513015735bfdcd26b2:
You offer all the money you brought, but the men only laugh.
— Keep those pennies. Crossing costs much more. Come back when you find real money.
You realize it's dangerous to stay here, so you retreat as fast as you can.
ch.68743e552dc86106b95ea59a:
The only valuable thing you have is the ring you found on the battlefield. Maybe you wanted to keep it, but getting to Targrad matters more. You are ready to part with it. Still, handing something so valuable to just anyone is foolish. You ask to be taken to their leader. The men exchange glances and reluctantly agree.
— Do not twitch, or we will cut you like a pig. — one says, and you nod. You really have no choice either way.
ch.68743e5f9b0310596ad63511: You return to the village and look around. A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with a tray full of various sausages and pieces of dried meat. Both are trying hard to lure you to their goods.
ch.68743e83a2b300463c0b3c0f:
They lead you into the outpost. You notice old, dark bloodstains on the walls — looks like bodies once lay there.
In the former guardroom a powerfully built man meets you. He does not take off his helmet, he only turns toward you. A hammer lies within his reach. He could easily grab it and smash your head if you do something stupid.
— Who is this? — the chief's voice is muffled by the helmet.
— Says he wants to cross. Wants to pay you.
— Well then, show what you have. —  the chief is staring at you. You quickly pull out the ring.
ch.68743e92edbae8910c70e855:
You decide you should talk to scum like this accordingly.
— I have the right to pass through this outpost in the name of the Order of the Navigators!
Only your plan does not work in the slightest. There is not a trace of fear on the faces before you, only anger.
— Oh yeah? Anything else you wanna share? — the men close in and draw their weapons.
ch.68743ea9a3cfe66f514a2b7b: "You are obliged to let me through!"
ch.687443b629bc4666cdbdbf7e:
You remember the ring you found and show it. The men calm down at once, though they do not lower their weapons.
— Should have said so from the start. Come with us, you can give the payment to the chief.
ch.687443ef1372b57f63ea8ba0:
You square your shoulders and press your lips together. You feel you need to stand your ground. It is the only way these bandits will get the message.
Only they are not in the mood to understand anything.
— Who do you think you are?!
One of the men advances on you with a bare sword. Looks like you really managed to anger them. You dodge the first strike, slip away from the second, but the third catches you.
Horrifying pain burns as the blade rips open your stomach. Your insides slip under your fingers when you instinctively grab the wound. The very thought of touching your own guts makes you stagger. Or maybe it's the pain?
ch.687443f433e205ef73e9f3d0: You fall to the ground, clutching your stomach. The stench is vile; everything around is covered with your blood. Your head spins and you close your eyes.
ch.68744421f2028b28ea419f87: Hold the ring back for now.
ch.687444455dc8d2e45c7dbfe1:
You hesitate. Will they throw you out the moment you show the ring? You freeze, gripping it tightly in your fist.
The chief clearly does not like that.
He strides up with a soldier’s quick step and grabs you by the scruff like a kitten. Your collar bites into your throat and steals your breath.
— You come here asking me to let you cross and you are clutching the payment?! Who do you think you are?!
ch.68744449d9f37dbfbf13e107:
You decide not to risk it and hold the ring out on your open palm. The chief stomps closer and snatches it. Lifting his hand, he snorts as he studies the ring.
— Nice trinket. Worth a lot. Where did you get it? Although, doesn't matter.
He pockets the ring and looks at you.
— Password?
ch.6874453917d74962c58b3e39:
— The usual one! We won't et you through without it.
The man pockets the ring and turns away from you.
— Don't come back until you learn the password.
They lead you out of the guardroom and shove you out of the outpost.
ch.68744546795167b8dd7e1ebd:
You feel the chief’s gaze on you, even though you cannot see his face. He lets the silence stretch, obviously to make you nervous. You wait calmly.
— Hell knows how you know the password, but it is correct. — he whistles to his men and nods at you. — Escort him.
ch.687445aa419f9d2b6f4582f1:
The butcher perks up the instant he sees you heading his way.
— Ha, we have not had guests in a good while!
You want to ask how he knows you are not local, but he talks first.
— Our village is small. I know everyone. So, are you buying anything?
ch.687445c5251abe1b4f2aa90d:
You decide to take something for the road. A small hunk of sausage will do.
— Great choice! My wife makes it, she's got golden hands! You will not regret it.
The vendor neatly slices off a piece and hands it to you.
ch.687445d8445e961ec32c599c:
You shake your head, and the vendor presses his lips in annoyance. He clearly hoped to peddle something to you. You, however, are not hungry and do not want to spend money.
— Well then, safe travels.
You get the feeling he would be happy to wish you the opposite.
ch.687445f4f684e8fb354425cb: The man won't tell you anything now. You should try your luck with the milk seller woman.
ch.687445faa444ba5c8d9c1376: You should ask about the garrison. That is why you came here.
ch.68744664350e1c269449a1c3:
You pay for the food, and the vendor quickly tucks the coins into his purse.
— What brings you to our village?
The man has relaxed since you bought the sausage. This is your chance to learn something about the outpost.
ch.6874467952382aa9a2335664: What about that outpost at the river?
ch.687446888ec9d6fe0e20054c:
The man shrugs and gestures toward the woman with the milk.
— Those are not our people out there anymore. Nastasya will tell you more than I can, even if you don't buy anything from her. She's always ready to chat.
ch.687446a17a50590644cb2e0f:
You say goodbye to the butcher and head to the woman, smiling politely. She knows what you need.
— Well now, what handsome fellow has dropped by our village! — she grins wide. She is missing a tooth. — Here for milk or for a chat?
ch.687446a7de4662956ea7000c:
You feel like this man might know something else, and your hunch is right. The moment you fall silent, he leans in and whispers conspiratorially.
— There is some kind of evil spirit in our well. Along with the water you get strange prophecies. Everyone sees their own version.
ch.687446ca5dadd51c3ab2e0a1: From his reaction you can tell he will not say anything more, at least nothing useful. You missed your chance by not buying anything.
ch.687446d60c21751530b7c21c:
— And that garrison at the river... What happened to it? — you ask casually. The vendor frowns and gives a nervous shrug.

— Well... There were decent lads there once, used to visit our girls often. Then those thugs showed up, — she presses her lips in displeasure, — and that was that. The lads are gone.
cz.6889fd43911515e43c8c2b3a:
— I... I know the password.
The knowledge surfaces in your mind as if on its own, but you do not doubt it. The password is correct.
— Really? Then go on, say it.
The man is eyeing you with suspicion.
cz.6889fd4e0ed088c592ca24cf: You are furious. What damn password?! Did the elder trick you? You need to find out right now. Or should you risk it and try to break through?

— No, dear, don’t. Consider it my treat. We like travelers here.

You feel awkward, but you agree. You don’t feel like arguing at all. You take the mug and sip. You’ve never tasted milk this good. You finish it all and wipe your mouth with your sleeve.

— Like it, don't'cha? — the woman laughs. You nod. The woman is in high spirits now. Maybe she’ll share something useful.

— It’s been a long time since we’ve had anyone here. Ever since what happened with the outpost…
cz.6890d638706bcdd070129ba3: You are furious. What damn password?! Did the elder trick you? You need to find out right now. Or should you risk it and try to break through?

cz.689c601038b1721d40107a3b: You have already been to the battlefield and saw the ring the elder wants so badly. You should have taken it then, but oh well.
cz.689c604096749cc24fa89d85: You have already been to the battlefield, but saw no ring. Then again, you did not look for one.
cz.689c6072aea239d5c19750ee:

The fallen warrior lies on ground soaked with blood. You crouch beside him, ready this time to take the ring.
cz.689c61411a52f71a5611a1aa:

You look around. Where should you search for the ring?

cz.689c62effc2cb2251deced4a:
You focus on several corpses lying on the blood-soaked ground, then come closer. One man with richer clothing catches your attention.

You crouch beside him. The stench of sun-baked bodies hits you harder. You hold your breath while you examine the dead man’s hands.

You find the ring quickly.
cz.689c98bbb8a0111a4ac7f1fb: Appease the dog with the sausage.
cz.689c98c3a9d3088c05acab1e:

The piece of sausage you pull from your pack flies over the fence. The dog flinches at first, then, catching the scent, edges closer. It grabs the food like it has not been fed in years.
cz.689c997a10ec4dc751719b80: The dog is busy with its windfall, which means the way to the house is open. You carefully open the gate and step inside.
cz.689c9a769cdf67444b65e317:

— What is this? Feeding my dog? How is he supposed to guard then? He cannot do it on a full belly!

He kicks the dog, driving it away from the sausage. It yelps but obediently backs off, staring greedily at the leftover chunk.

— But I will praise your wits, — the elder says, looking you over, then nods behind himself. — Come inside. Tell me what you came for.
cz.689c9abe2757883b7baa7ad0:
You go inside with the elder. It is warm and smells of fresh bread. He does not offer you a seat.

— Who are you and where are you headed? I have not seen you in the village before.
cz.689f4847426c274c0b679373: You look at the man standing in front of you and realize it’s not worth the risk. They’d just kill you without a second thought. No, better to visit the elder again and ask what kind of game he’s playing.
cz.689f489c146f270489c38257:
You leave the elder empty-handed. Now what? Where are you supposed to find this damn password?

There’s got to be more to this than it seems. If you dig deep enough, you’ll find a way forward. This whole world feels like it’s made of nothing but puzzles. But isn’t that what makes it more exciting?

You know you need to think. Maybe you should rest. Or maybe turn to one of your friends outside your path for help.
cz.689f48de3b47a5cc734addec:
You don’t have time to run back and forth chasing down some password. So you decide to act.

You lunge forward, shoving the man out of your way. He clearly didn’t expect that kind of boldness and doesn’t react right away. You sprint ahead, slipping through the gate of the outpost.
cz.689f4912e84e2561e5645f50:
You keep going, bursting through the gate.

Ahead of you lies a tiny courtyard, and just beyond it the bridge to the other side. Your goal is so close!

But the outpost isn’t guarded by just the man you left behind. In the courtyard, a few others are playing cards. The moment they spot you, they leap to their feet and grab their weapons.

— Where the hell do you think you’re going?! — one of them curses, then whistles sharply.
cz.689f49e9948b799c4f33d808:
You have no choice but to go all in.

Like a berserker, you dash forward, yelling, half to scare the bandits, half to steel yourself.

But you only make it halfway across the courtyard.
cz.689f49fb899498a7be9cac58:
You freeze, unsure what to do. Run back? No, that’s stupid. Forward? You don’t even have a weapon!

Not that you get the chance to decide.
cz.689f4a07239f2965c3c6c828:
You decide to turn back. Clearly, you’ve overestimated yourself.

You raise your hands, force a guilty smile, and step back. You don’t even manage to say a word in your defense.
cz.689f4bc7037746c8a7d97cf4:
Suddenly, you hear a faint whistle, and a moment later something slams into your shoulder. The pain feels like someone’s trying to rip your arm clean off. Instinctively, you clutch the wound with your hand.

An arrow hits you.

You scream like a cornered animal, begging them to stop, but the third arrow punches straight through your skull.

You collapse lifelessly. On your nameless grave they’ll write “Brave, but foolish”.
cz.689f534cb15f1c44c281c955: You pull a gold coin from your pouch and toss it neatly into the dark mouth of the well. A second later you expect to hear a splash, but nothing comes. Is it really that deep?

cz.689f55668f28d43762e2a816:
You shrug and toss another coin into the well. This time, something shiny shoots back up and smacks you square in the forehead before bouncing back down.

Now you hear a splash.

The well just threw your coin at you! Or whatever lives inside it did.
cz.689f5623416da0ee0dccbce0: Better not risk it again. Play it safe.
cz.689f5649a4982cf97fab12ab: Figure out what happened. Curiosity wins!
cz.689f565d0e328e5fac59c293:
You peer inside and see nothing but darkness. Deep, deep below, you can hear water splashing. Suddenly, a strange ringing sound rises from the depths.

You lean lower, trying to catch sight of its source.

en.68743d0df285ae400d661914:
After a few hours of unhurried walking, you see the first modest houses.

Your route passes through a tiny village. Once it thrived from trade coming from Targrad, but the war changed everything. Now there are fewer traders, less money. People are leaving. The road to Targrad isn’t long, but maybe it’s worth at least replenishing your water supplies?
en.68743d72e63583c86c178242: Yes, it's best to stay here for a bit.
en.68743d766f1e35975767990e: No, you have everything you need. Better hurry.
en.68743d7bcb8ce2f65f19987e: You realize you have not eaten in a long time. And your water ran out last night. There is nowhere to resupply between here and Targrad, so it makes sense to stop.
en.68743d808cc2bdc17eb7d442: You are not going to waste time. You have enough water, and you can grab a bite once you reach Targrad. The message is more important right now.
en.68743d83ef859469e1da95d7: A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with chunks of meat. Both are working hard to draw you to their goods.
en.68743d89f31067886c0f6235:
You walk straight through the village, not stopping anywhere. Today looks like market day: various goods are laid throughout the village's center. The locals watch you with a hint of hope, wishing you would buy something. You just keep walking.
At last, an outpost with a bridge over the river appears ahead. But something is off. No Targrad pennants, no guards... You stop just in time to notice men at the gate. Their armor is battered, their looks unkempt. They are definitely not soldiers. Goosebumps run down your back.
en.68743dbb7c48f120d1b53172: You should probably go back to the village and ask the locals who they are and where the garrison went.
en.68743dc0a13b10e7875570b0:
You retreat as quickly as you can. The men do not notice you. You have no idea what they are doing there, where the Targrad guards went, or how you are supposed to cross now...
You return to the village and look around. A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with a tray full of various sausages and pieces of dried meat. Both are trying hard to lure you to their goods.
en.68743dff32194b7a514624e5:
The men spot you quickly, perk up, and shout,
— Hey you, what are you doing here? C'mere!
You come closer.
The men are armed and look hostile.
— So why're you here? Cat got your tongue? We can help you pull it out!
en.68743e03f6173c9e91a166a0: You don't want to fight. Answer calmly.
en.68743e07116888f39aef1d7e: Who do they think they are? You have a permit from the head of the Order to pass through all these lands!
en.68743e231723328dcfa13297:
You lift your chin and walk straight toward the men. They notice you, exchange looks, and frown.
— So, why are you here? Need to get to the other side?
You nod.
— Then pay.
They smirk. One of them holds out his hand. You realize your travel charter signed by the head of the Order will not help here.
en.68743e259520db6ad8760da8: Whoever they are, you need to get to the other side of the river. You will go to them by yourself.
en.68743e337348f6ea87d4816f:
— I need to get to the other side.
Yes, a very diplomatic answer!
— Then pay.
en.68743e513015735bfdcd26b2:
You offer all the money you brought, but the men only laugh.
— Keep those pennies. Crossing costs much more. Come back when you find real money.
You realize it's dangerous to stay here, so you retreat as fast as you can.
en.68743e552dc86106b95ea59a:
The only valuable thing you have is the ring you found on the battlefield. Maybe you wanted to keep it, but getting to Targrad matters more. You are ready to part with it. Still, handing something so valuable to just anyone is foolish. You ask to be taken to their leader. The men exchange glances and reluctantly agree.
— Do not twitch, or we will cut you like a pig. — one says, and you nod. You really have no choice either way.
en.68743e5f9b0310596ad63511: You return to the village and look around. A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with a tray full of various sausages and pieces of dried meat. Both are trying hard to lure you to their goods.
en.68743e83a2b300463c0b3c0f:
They lead you into the outpost. You notice old, dark bloodstains on the walls — looks like bodies once lay there.
In the former guardroom a powerfully built man meets you. He does not take off his helmet, he only turns toward you. A hammer lies within his reach. He could easily grab it and smash your head if you do something stupid.
— Who is this? — the chief's voice is muffled by the helmet.
— Says he wants to cross. Wants to pay you.
— Well then, show what you have. —  the chief is staring at you. You quickly pull out the ring.
en.68743e92edbae8910c70e855:
You decide you should talk to scum like this accordingly.
— I have the right to pass through this outpost in the name of the Order of the Navigators!
Only your plan does not work in the slightest. There is not a trace of fear on the faces before you, only anger.
— Oh yeah? Anything else you wanna share? — the men close in and draw their weapons.
en.68743ea9a3cfe66f514a2b7b: "You are obliged to let me through!"
en.687443b629bc4666cdbdbf7e:
You remember the ring you found and show it. The men calm down at once, though they do not lower their weapons.
— Should have said so from the start. Come with us, you can give the payment to the chief.
en.687443ef1372b57f63ea8ba0:
You square your shoulders and press your lips together. You feel you need to stand your ground. It is the only way these bandits will get the message.
Only they are not in the mood to understand anything.
— Who do you think you are?!
One of the men advances on you with a bare sword. Looks like you really managed to anger them. You dodge the first strike, slip away from the second, but the third catches you.
Horrifying pain burns as the blade rips open your stomach. Your insides slip under your fingers when you instinctively grab the wound. The very thought of touching your own guts makes you stagger. Or maybe it's the pain?
en.687443f433e205ef73e9f3d0: You fall to the ground, clutching your stomach. The stench is vile; everything around is covered with your blood. Your head spins and you close your eyes.
en.68744421f2028b28ea419f87: Hold the ring back for now.
en.687444455dc8d2e45c7dbfe1:
You hesitate. Will they throw you out the moment you show the ring? You freeze, gripping it tightly in your fist.
The chief clearly does not like that.
He strides up with a soldier’s quick step and grabs you by the scruff like a kitten. Your collar bites into your throat and steals your breath.
— You come here asking me to let you cross and you are clutching the payment?! Who do you think you are?!
en.68744449d9f37dbfbf13e107:
You decide not to risk it and hold the ring out on your open palm. The chief stomps closer and snatches it. Lifting his hand, he snorts as he studies the ring.
— Nice trinket. Worth a lot. Where did you get it? Although, doesn't matter.
He pockets the ring and looks at you.
— Password?
en.6874453917d74962c58b3e39:

The man pockets the ring and turns away from you.
— Don't come back until you learn the password.
They lead you out of the guardroom and shove you out of the outpost.
en.68744546795167b8dd7e1ebd:
You feel the chief’s gaze on you, even though you cannot see his face. He lets the silence stretch, obviously to make you nervous. You wait calmly.
— Hell knows how you know the password, but it is correct. — he whistles to his men and nods at you. — Escort him.
en.687445aa419f9d2b6f4582f1:
The butcher perks up the instant he sees you heading his way.

en.687445c5251abe1b4f2aa90d:

en.687446e4f58e359b0d29f644: Better talk to the milk seller woman. Maybe she knows something.

en.6874486655062c766eb05024: Down below there is only darkness and faint gleams on the water. You do not lean over the lip, you only peek with one eye. Suddenly a ringing rises from the depths. Maybe the spirit is trying to distract you, but you keep your cool.
en.6874486b1ec0d473850ace76:
Suddenly, multiple hands appear out of the dark. You notice sharp claws and scales, a bluish sheen to the skin, but you do not have time to jump back.
The hands grab your clothes and bite into the soft skin of your throat. Something pulls you down into the well.
— It is all because of you. Because of you we all died, will die, and will keep dying!
You hear a furious whisper and cry out.
— I did not do anything! — you shout, but the monster only pulls harder. You tear your nails trying to save yourself, but nothing helps.
You fall and fall and fall until you hit the water.
en.68744881ff9637da0559e6d1:
That is exactly what saves you when the ghoulish hands appear from the dark. You manage to see the sharp claws, the corpse’s bluish skin, the scales. Acting on instinct, you jump back and fall. The hands clutch the rim of the well and stay there. Someone whimpers, then a voice speaks.
— Because of you we all died, will die, and will keep dying. Over and over, over and over. You are death itself for these lands.
en.687448f58341a32358ea076b:
The voice seems to split and layer over itself. You hear very young voices, bright and cheerful, and old ones, creaky and worn. You do not move — you only watch and listen.
— We will all die. The paper… Cannot. Must not open.
The spirit slides its fingers along the rim and scratches the wood with its claws.
— You must die so that we can all live.
Suddenly the hands disappear. Something splashes in the distance. Someone sighs. You hear the fading words: "we are all doomed".
And then silence.
en.6874490e17fd456833550cad:

— What are you talking about? I only just arrived in this village.
The spirit’s hands shoot up and rake the rim, as if trying to reach you.
— You are death itself. You should have died, fallen from the ladder. You must not reach Targrad. You must not open the seal.
The thing in the well rages, tears at the rim, growls, moans, and cries.
— We will all die because of you. All of us, all of us will die.
Suddenly the hands vanish. There is a splash somewhere in the depths. You hear the fading words: "we are all doomed".
And then silence.
en.6874492a76b6092cc64498f8: You barely have time to think "to hell with this" before your body moves on its own. You scramble back and jump to your feet, never taking your eyes off the well. The hands still lie on the rim, the words echo from the depths, but you do not care. You run away headlong.
en.68744935d64af04f28293440: The world around you comes alive again. All the sounds return, birds sing, children laugh. The sun warms your head. You realize the spirit has truly gone. en.687449e8fd2ff21599061ca3:
You approach the milk seller with a friendly smile. She might know something, so it is best to be nice. Friendly talk loosens tongues.

— Well now, what handsome fellow has dropped by our village! — she grins wide. She is missing a tooth. — Here for milk or for a chat?

en.68744abdc69bc430bc57648d: "Why not write to the city so they send their warriors to deal with it?"
en.68744ac56159d48cac2bb0c1:

— But I think the elder is the one who called them. They're his buddies. He gets a bit of share from them. And we only part with our money because of his scheme!
en.68744aeb5780841b5fcba45e:
— I would write if I could. Only our elder knows how, and he is not writing for some reason. Says it is better with them. They protect us better than those Targrad guards, he says! But in reality, they just shake people down at the crossing.

— He made a deal with them. Maybe he called them himself. Well it's good for him, he gets some coin. And us? Nothing!
en.68744af23ea3fc927bbb841a: She keeps talking, and you realize the only person who can help you cross the river is the elder. You need to visit him.
en.68744ba15c1e3b546f6fd896:

In the yard, behind a sturdy fence, a dog greets you with loud barking. It jumps at the fence, trying to reach you.
en.68744bd2fd705cffd2ccfce9: Some mutt is not going to scare you! Stand your ground.
en.68744bdd7d59af6c9f982583: You stare down the barking dog. Not a muscle twitches on your face. It will not reach you, so you aren't afraid. You have seen worse things than some mutt.

— Who might you be?
You are about to answer when the elder raises a hand.
— Come inside. We will talk there. The gate is open, come in.
en.68744c07ba326767b8236230: The dog, as if noticing you don't care about its efforts, growls and flattens to the ground. In a heartbeat it vaults the fence and sinks its teeth into your arm. Pain engulfs you. You jerk back, try to shake the dog off, but nothing works. The jaws are locked.
en.68744c1d9f97f7b96553ce1c:
— Buddy, back! Sit!
Your savior appears from the house. The dog releases you at once, jumps aside, and wags its tail. You really want to kick it, but you do not dare in front of the owner.
— Good boy, a real guardian! — the man says as he opens the gate and ushers the dog back in. Looking over your arm, he clicks his tongue.
— Apologies. The dog is just doing his job. Come inside, let's see your arm.
en.68744c3b2942a0c5bc6a9281:
You push the gate and walk toward the door. The dog watches you but does not attack, as if it understands its master invited you in.

Inside is warm and smells of fresh bread. The elder does not offer you a seat.

— Who are you and where are you headed? I have not seen you in the village before.
en.68744c6dd76753d904aa625f:
Inside, the man, obviously the village elder, examines your arm. The dog did not bite down to the bone, there isn't much blood. The bite aches but is nothing serious. He wraps it with a strip of linen himself.
— You'll live, don't worry. Why did you come here?
en.68744c87867ad25c390a84d5:
You explain you need to get to Targrad and mention the crossing. The elder smirks and folds his arms across his chest.
— My friends are posted there now. They do not let anyone through, and if they do, they ask for gold. I can help you if you help me.
en.68744cb6a8b8ead414941f3e: "What is stopping me from going around the crossing and finding another way?"
en.68744cc1bf880f745acfde1b: "I'll help. I really need to get to the other side."
en.68744ccceea62ee263f785c9:
The elder smiles in an unpleasant way and laughs.
— If you have three days to spare, you can try to reach the nearest ford. But spring was rough this year, it might have been washed out...
You realize you do not really have a choice.
en.68744d0e1c15534d022dfe5d:
— Not long ago there was a battle nearby. Turva and Karhu crossed blades again. There was a young man, a noble. By rumor he ran away from Targrad to join the warriors. The battle was a couple of days ago, but that fellow and his men never returned.
The elder pauses to make sure you are listening.
You are listening.
— So. When that fellow was here, I noticed a nice ring on him. You need to find it.
en.68744d3aebecefbca7db3772:
— I like that attitude! — the elder smiles.
— Not long ago there was a battle nearby. Turva and Karhu crossed blades again. There was a young man, a noble. By rumor he ran away from Targrad to join the warriors. The battle was a couple of days ago, but that fellow and his men never returned.
The elder pauses to make sure you are listening.
You are listening.
— So. When that fellow was here, I noticed a nice ring on him. You need to find it.
en.68744d619aa1eed8a89eaad7: Is he talking about that one ring you found?
en.68744d63eec117ef73ba6c03: "Why do you not go look for it yourself?"
en.68744da90e2c0d98e8755c9a:
You take your travel pack off your back, open it, and rummage. The elder watches, puzzled.
At last you feel the ring and pull it out.
— Is this what you are looking for?
The elder’s eyes flare at once. He steps forward, unable to take his eyes off the ring.
— Yes, yes, that is it! You already visited the field, did you? — he smirks, then waves a hand. — Put it on the table. I will write a letter to the outpost so they let you pass.
en.68744db87e93a1c49671fc5f:
The elder snorts at your question.
— The battlefield is an open graveyard right now. And how would I look, walking among the dead and inspecting their hands? News travels fast in this village.
He looks at you with less warmth.
— That is all. Go now, don't waste my time.
en.68744dd2f735dbcfce093ee5: You realize you have no choice. You haven't brought much money with you, so you cannot pay for the crossing. You nod and leave the elder’s house. You will have to find that damn ring.
en.68744de936cd8129390158e3:
The battlefield greets you with a hundred simultaneous sounds. You always thought where death had passed there would be silence, but nature has no time for mourning. Besides, mourning whom? People who kill each other over petty grievances?

You look at the bodies, broken banners, and fallen weapons. You press your sleeve to your nose and mouth to keep the stench of death from dizzying you.
Your goal is the ring. But where could it be?
en.68744dff019ab01607f0341b: Maybe that noble was pinned by the dead horse?
en.68744e0f4742b1fd2654d01f: You approach the bodies lying on the ground. A light breeze blows, letting you inhale without the stench of decay. Now you can examine the bodies.
en.68744e13d70299f5be4f9d97:
You approach the horse. The smell is suffocating and sharp, making your eyes water. You look at the poor animal and the broken cart nearby. War shows no mercy to anyone, not even animals.
You circle the carcass and realize there is no rider here, and never was. You should search the bodies.
en.68744e211a6f316024bec831:
You move closer. It hasn’t rained in a long time, so the ground is dry and dusty. Next to the bodies, the grass is stained with dried blood. Even in this proximity, the wind doesn’t mask the scent.
Your gaze slides over the fallen.
en.68744e3d12d8003f9a04617c: Saddening. They still had life ahead of them.
en.68744e4c2d6dd1bbdf590aad:
You shake your head, looking at the bodies with sorrow. War spares no one, neither the young nor the old.
Suddenly, your attention is drawn to the ring on one of the dead men.
en.68744e50a6ccdab5d239cacb:
You purse your lips, looking at the bodies. You feel no pity: these people chose this path. Any warrior risks ending up a corpse among crows.
Your eyes sweep over the fallen, and you notice the glint of a ring on one of them.
en.68744e6be27317358e8256eb: You crouch near the body. The corpse lies in an unnatural position, but his eyes are closed and his face is peaceful. You immediately notice that the man’s clothing is richer than the others’. This is clearly the noble the elder talked about.
en.68744e79f371bc88f8874284:
You look around, as if someone might see you. You’ve never stolen anything, but... the owner of the ring is already dead, he doesn’t need it anymore, but you need it to get to Targrad...
You remove the ring from the lifeless hand.
It feels as if the corpse might squeeze his hand and growl, but nothing happens. You simply take the ring and place it in your bag. Now you can return to the village.
en.68744eac4e39769d76e127ba:
You head straight back to the elder’s house. The dog is tied this time and does not even bark — seems like it remembers you. You enter. The elder rises from the bench to meet you, somewhat surprised.
— That was quick! Did you find it?
You nod and hand him the ring. You want to get rid of it and leave the village as soon as possible.
He takes the ring and nods at the bench.
— Sit for a bit. I will write a letter to my friends at the outpost. Hand it over and they will let you through.
en.68744edd1969ad595dada20e:
You approach the crossing with the elder’s letter in hand. This time you feel confident and do not even flinch when they shout. You hand the letter to the man who comes out.

He turns the paper over and over, spits, and takes it somewhere inside.

— Wait here.

About ten minutes later he returns.

— Turn around. — he hands crosses his arms, — Now beat it.
en.68744ff5d8199af339657f71:
You return to the elder’s house. The dog on the threshold lifts its head in surprise. Seems like it did not expect to see you again.

You burst into the house. The elder jumps up at once and frowns. You demand the password.

— What password? There was no password! — he is not a good liar. — Think about it. Why would I do that? I got what I wanted. I do not need you here. I know no passwords. Now get out of my house.
en.6874501cea1c4db9c71af471:
— All right... The password's correct. — the man at the crossing frowns. Looks like he wanted to mess with you a bit more for fun. But you said the correct word, so there is no point dragging it out.
He waves a hand.
— Come on. I will have you escorted to the other bank.
en.688025ef531ad6db72b2c808:
You hand the ring to the chief. He lets you go at once, snatches the trinket, and studies it through the slits of his helmet.
— Should've done that from the start. — The ring disappears into his belt pouch. — Now say the password.
en.68804766a0a3ac4e44f67ef8: — Nah, the letter's good. — the man grins and spits at your feet. — But there is no password. We will not let you through without a password.
en.6880476bb4dbb927ddb14064: — Of course not! — the man grins and spits at your feet. — You have no password. We will not let you through without a password.
en.6880bedb58b9a5498e6bdd2c:
The milk seller’s face shifts and she sighs.

— Well... There were decent lads there once, used to visit our girls often. Then those thugs showed up, — she presses her lips in displeasure, — and that was that. The lads are gone.
en.6889fd43911515e43c8c2b3a:
— I... I know the password.
The knowledge surfaces in your mind as if on its own, but you do not doubt it. The password is correct.
— Really? Then go on, say it.
The man is eyeing you with suspicion.
en.6889fd4e0ed088c592ca24cf: You are furious. What damn password?! Did the elder trick you? You need to find out right now. Or should you risk it and try to break through?
en.688f6f789239f3326bfce390:
The merchant woman quickly pours you some milk into a wooden mug and hands it over. You reach for money, but the woman shakes her head.

— No, dear, don’t. Consider it my treat. We like travelers here.

You feel awkward, but you agree. You don’t feel like arguing at all. You take the mug and sip. You’ve never tasted milk this good. You finish it all and wipe your mouth with your sleeve.

— Like it, don't'cha? — the woman laughs. You nod. The woman is in high spirits now. Maybe she’ll share something useful.

— It’s been a long time since we’ve had anyone here. Ever since what happened with the outpost…
en.6890d638706bcdd070129ba3: You are furious. What damn password?! Did the elder trick you? You need to find out right now. Or should you risk it and try to break through?
en.68947a502b9c1677632cbd7a:
You pay for the food, and the vendor quickly tucks the coins into his purse.
— What brings you to our village?
The man has clearly relaxed after you bought a slice of sausage. This is your chance to learn something about the outpost.
en.689c601038b1721d40107a3b: You have already been to the battlefield and saw the ring the elder wants so badly. You should have taken it then, but oh well.
en.689c604096749cc24fa89d85: You have already been to the battlefield, but saw no ring. Then again, you did not look for one.
en.689c6072aea239d5c19750ee:
The battlefield greets you with a hundred sounds at once. Nothinmg changed while you were, except the smell is now stronger. You wince, roll your shoulders, and head straight for the bodies. No point delaying.

The fallen warrior lies on ground soaked with blood. You crouch beside him, ready this time to take the ring.
en.689c61411a52f71a5611a1aa:
You return to the battlefield. It greets you with a hundred sounds and a horrible stench. You have to cover your nose and mouth with your sleeve.

You look around. Where should you search for the ring?
en.689c614d91a5f755532ca989: Last time you only examined the dead horse, then left. There will definitely be no rings by it.
en.689c6201741098dfb19e53af: Maybe that noble was pinned by the horse?
en.689c62effc2cb2251deced4a:
You focus on several corpses lying on the blood-soaked ground, then come closer. One man with richer clothing catches your attention.

You crouch beside him. The stench of sun-baked bodies hits you harder. You hold your breath while you examine the dead man’s hands.

You find the ring quickly.
en.689c98bbb8a0111a4ac7f1fb: Appease the dog with the sausage.
en.689c98c3a9d3088c05acab1e:
You wanted to eat the sausage yourself later, but the situation calls for sacrifice. You are ready to make it.

The piece of sausage you pull from your pack flies over the fence. The dog flinches at first, then, catching the scent, edges closer. It grabs the food like it has not been fed in years.
en.689c997a10ec4dc751719b80: The dog is busy with its windfall, which means the way to the house is open. You carefully open the gate and step inside.
en.689c9a769cdf67444b65e317:
A man comes out of the house. He looks around forty — tall, broad-shouldered, with a belly taut under his shirt. You immediately understand this is the village elder.

— What is this? Feeding my dog? How is he supposed to guard then? He cannot do it on a full belly!

He kicks the dog, driving it away from the sausage. It yelps but obediently backs off, staring greedily at the leftover chunk.

— But I will praise your wits, — the elder says, looking you over, then nods behind himself. — Come inside. Tell me what you came for.
en.689c9abe2757883b7baa7ad0:
You go inside with the elder. It is warm and smells of fresh bread. He does not offer you a seat.

— Who are you and where are you headed? I have not seen you in the village before.
en.689f4847426c274c0b679373: You look at the man standing in front of you and realize it’s not worth the risk. They’d just kill you without a second thought. No, better to visit the elder again and ask what kind of game he’s playing.
en.689f489c146f270489c38257:
You leave the elder empty-handed. Now what? Where are you supposed to find this damn password?

There’s got to be more to this than it seems. If you dig deep enough, you’ll find a way forward. This whole world feels like it’s made of nothing but puzzles. But isn’t that what makes it more exciting?

You know you need to think. Maybe you should rest. Or maybe turn to one of your friends outside your path for help.
en.689f48de3b47a5cc734addec:
You don’t have time to run back and forth chasing down some password. So you decide to act.

You lunge forward, shoving the man out of your way. He clearly didn’t expect that kind of boldness and doesn’t react right away. You sprint ahead, slipping through the gate of the outpost.
en.689f4912e84e2561e5645f50:
You keep going, bursting through the gate.

Ahead of you lies a tiny courtyard, and just beyond it the bridge to the other side. Your goal is so close!

But the outpost isn’t guarded by just the man you left behind. In the courtyard, a few others are playing cards. The moment they spot you, they leap to their feet and grab their weapons.

— Where the hell do you think you’re going?! — one of them curses, then whistles sharply.
en.689f49e9948b799c4f33d808:
You have no choice but to go all in.

Like a berserker, you dash forward, yelling, half to scare the bandits, half to steel yourself.

But you only make it halfway across the courtyard.
en.689f49fb899498a7be9cac58:
You freeze, unsure what to do. Run back? No, that’s stupid. Forward? You don’t even have a weapon!

Not that you get the chance to decide.
en.689f4a07239f2965c3c6c828:
You decide to turn back. Clearly, you’ve overestimated yourself.

You raise your hands, force a guilty smile, and step back. You don’t even manage to say a word in your defense.
en.689f4bc7037746c8a7d97cf4:
Suddenly, you hear a faint whistle, and a moment later something slams into your shoulder. The pain feels like someone’s trying to rip your arm clean off. Instinctively, you clutch the wound with your hand.

An arrow hits you.
en.689f4c18548d732e5c77d7b4:
But before you can even catch your breath, another arrow strikes you from the other side. This one buries itself in your thigh, and you stumble, dropping to one knee.

You scream like a cornered animal, begging them to stop, but the third arrow punches straight through your skull.

You collapse lifelessly. On your nameless grave they’ll write “Brave, but foolish”.
en.689f534cb15f1c44c281c955: You pull a gold coin from your pouch and toss it neatly into the dark mouth of the well. A second later you expect to hear a splash, but nothing comes. Is it really that deep?
en.689f535ba0d559d825f5fc89: Strange. Better play it safe and step back.
en.689f55668f28d43762e2a816:
You shrug and toss another coin into the well. This time, something shiny shoots back up and smacks you square in the forehead before bouncing back down.

Now you hear a splash.

The well just threw your coin at you! Or whatever lives inside it did.
en.689f5623416da0ee0dccbce0: Better not risk it again. Play it safe.
en.689f5649a4982cf97fab12ab: Figure out what happened. Curiosity wins!
en.689f565d0e328e5fac59c293:
You peer inside and see nothing but darkness. Deep, deep below, you can hear water splashing. Suddenly, a strange ringing sound rises from the depths.

You lean lower, trying to catch sight of its source.
en.689f569a18e77852b9b84b0f:
You pay for the food, and the vendor quickly tucks the coins into his purse.
— What brings you to our village?
The man has relaxed since you bought the sausage. This is your chance to learn something about the outpost.
en.689f56ae130f4eb0fbb5ac9e:
You pay for the food, and the vendor quickly tucks the coins into his purse.
— What brings you to our village?
The man has relaxed since you bought the sausage. This is your chance to learn something about the outpost.

es.68743d0df285ae400d661914:
After a few hours of unhurried walking, you see the first modest houses.

Your route passes through a tiny village. Once it thrived from trade coming from Targrad, but the war changed everything. Now there are fewer traders, less money. People are leaving. The road to Targrad isn’t long, but maybe it’s worth at least replenishing your water supplies?
es.68743d72e63583c86c178242: Yes, it's best to stay here for a bit.
es.68743d766f1e35975767990e: No, you have everything you need. Better hurry.
es.68743d7bcb8ce2f65f19987e: You realize you have not eaten in a long time. And your water ran out last night. There is nowhere to resupply between here and Targrad, so it makes sense to stop.
es.68743d808cc2bdc17eb7d442: You are not going to waste time. You have enough water, and you can grab a bite once you reach Targrad. The message is more important right now.
es.68743d83ef859469e1da95d7: A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with chunks of meat. Both are working hard to draw you to their goods.
es.68743d89f31067886c0f6235:
You walk straight through the village, not stopping anywhere. Today looks like market day: various goods are laid throughout the village's center. The locals watch you with a hint of hope, wishing you would buy something. You just keep walking.
At last, an outpost with a bridge over the river appears ahead. But something is off. No Targrad pennants, no guards... You stop just in time to notice men at the gate. Their armor is battered, their looks unkempt. They are definitely not soldiers. Goosebumps run down your back.
es.68743dbb7c48f120d1b53172: You should probably go back to the village and ask the locals who they are and where the garrison went.
es.68743dc0a13b10e7875570b0:
You retreat as quickly as you can. The men do not notice you. You have no idea what they are doing there, where the Targrad guards went, or how you are supposed to cross now...
You return to the village and look around. A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with a tray full of various sausages and pieces of dried meat. Both are trying hard to lure you to their goods.
es.68743dff32194b7a514624e5:
The men spot you quickly, perk up, and shout,
— Hey you, what are you doing here? C'mere!
You come closer.
The men are armed and look hostile.
— So why're you here? Cat got your tongue? We can help you pull it out!
es.68743e03f6173c9e91a166a0: You don't want to fight. Answer calmly.
es.68743e07116888f39aef1d7e: Who do they think they are? You have a permit from the head of the Order to pass through all these lands!
es.68743e231723328dcfa13297:
You lift your chin and walk straight toward the men. They notice you, exchange looks, and frown.
— So, why are you here? Need to get to the other side?
You nod.
— Then pay.
They smirk. One of them holds out his hand. You realize your travel charter signed by the head of the Order will not help here.
es.68743e259520db6ad8760da8: Whoever they are, you need to get to the other side of the river. You will go to them by yourself.
es.68743e337348f6ea87d4816f:
— I need to get to the other side.
Yes, a very diplomatic answer!
— Then pay.
es.68743e513015735bfdcd26b2:
You offer all the money you brought, but the men only laugh.
— Keep those pennies. Crossing costs much more. Come back when you find real money.
You realize it's dangerous to stay here, so you retreat as fast as you can.
es.68743e552dc86106b95ea59a:
The only valuable thing you have is the ring you found on the battlefield. Maybe you wanted to keep it, but getting to Targrad matters more. You are ready to part with it. Still, handing something so valuable to just anyone is foolish. You ask to be taken to their leader. The men exchange glances and reluctantly agree.
— Do not twitch, or we will cut you like a pig. — one says, and you nod. You really have no choice either way.
es.68743e5f9b0310596ad63511: You return to the village and look around. A woman beside you is selling milk. Right across from her stands a man with a tray full of various sausages and pieces of dried meat. Both are trying hard to lure you to their goods.
es.68743e83a2b300463c0b3c0f:
They lead you into the outpost. You notice old, dark bloodstains on the walls — looks like bodies once lay there.
In the former guardroom a powerfully built man meets you. He does not take off his helmet, he only turns toward you. A hammer lies within his reach. He could easily grab it and smash your head if you do something stupid.
— Who is this? — the chief's voice is muffled by the helmet.
— Says he wants to cross. Wants to pay you.
— Well then, show what you have. —  the chief is staring at you. You quickly pull out the ring.
es.68743e92edbae8910c70e855:
You decide you should talk to scum like this accordingly.
— I have the right to pass through this outpost in the name of the Order of the Navigators!
Only your plan does not work in the slightest. There is not a trace of fear on the faces before you, only anger.
— Oh yeah? Anything else you wanna share? — the men close in and draw their weapons.
es.68743ea9a3cfe66f514a2b7b: "You are obliged to let me through!"
es.687443b629bc4666cdbdbf7e:
You remember the ring you found and show it. The men calm down at once, though they do not lower their weapons.
— Should have said so from the start. Come with us, you can give the payment to the chief.
es.687443ef1372b57f63ea8ba0:
You square your shoulders and press your lips together. You feel you need to stand your ground. It is the only way these bandits will get the message.
Only they are not in the mood to understand anything.
— Who do you think you are?!
One of the men advances on you with a bare sword. Looks like you really managed to anger them. You dodge the first strike, slip away from the second, but the third catches you.
Horrifying pain burns as the blade rips open your stomach. Your insides slip under your fingers when you instinctively grab the wound. The very thought of touching your own guts makes you stagger. Or maybe it's the pain?
es.687443f433e205ef73e9f3d0: You fall to the ground, clutching your stomach. The stench is vile; everything around is covered with your blood. Your head spins and you close your eyes.
es.68744421f2028b28ea419f87: Hold the ring back for now.
es.687444455dc8d2e45c7dbfe1:
You hesitate. Will they throw you out the moment you show the ring? You freeze, gripping it tightly in your fist.
The chief clearly does not like that.
He strides up with a soldier’s quick step and grabs you by the scruff like a kitten. Your collar bites into your throat and steals your breath.
— You come here asking me to let you cross and you are clutching the payment?! Who do you think you are?!
es.68744449d9f37dbfbf13e107:
You decide not to risk it and hold the ring out on your open palm. The chief stomps closer and snatches it. Lifting his hand, he snorts as he studies the ring.
— Nice trinket. Worth a lot. Where did you get it? Although, doesn't matter.
He pockets the ring and looks at you.
— Password?
es.6874453917d74962c58b3e39:
— The usual one! We won't et you through without it.
The man pockets the ring and turns away from you.
— Don't come back until you learn the password.
They lead you out of the guardroom and shove you out of the outpost.
es.68744546795167b8dd7e1ebd:
You feel the chief’s gaze on you, even though you cannot see his face. He lets the silence stretch, obviously to make you nervous. You wait calmly.
— Hell knows how you know the password, but it is correct. — he whistles to his men and nods at you. — Escort him.
es.687445aa419f9d2b6f4582f1:
The butcher perks up the instant he sees you heading his way.
— Ha, we have not had guests in a good while!
You want to ask how he knows you are not local, but he talks first.
— Our village is small. I know everyone. So, are you buying anything?
es.687445c5251abe1b4f2aa90d:
You decide to take something for the road. A small hunk of sausage will do.
— Great choice! My wife makes it, she's got golden hands! You will not regret it.
The vendor neatly slices off a piece and hands it to you.
es.687445d8445e961ec32c599c:
You shake your head, and the vendor presses his lips in annoyance. He clearly hoped to peddle something to you. You, however, are not hungry and do not want to spend money.
— Well then, safe travels.
You get the feeling he would be happy to wish you the opposite.
es.687445f4f684e8fb354425cb: The man won't tell you anything now. You should try your luck with the milk seller woman.
es.687445faa444ba5c8d9c1376: You should ask about the garrison. That is why you came here.
es.68744664350e1c269449a1c3:
You pay for the food, and the vendor quickly tucks the coins into his purse.
— What brings you to our village?
The man has relaxed since you bought the sausage. This is your chance to learn something about the outpost.
es.6874467952382aa9a2335664: What about that outpost at the river?
es.687446888ec9d6fe0e20054c:
The man shrugs and gestures toward the woman with the milk.
— Those are not our people out there anymore. Nastasya will tell you more than I can, even if you don't buy anything from her. She's always ready to chat.
es.687446a17a50590644cb2e0f:
You say goodbye to the butcher and head to the woman, smiling politely. She knows what you need.
— Well now, what handsome fellow has dropped by our village! — she grins wide. She is missing a tooth. — Here for milk or for a chat?
es.687446a7de4662956ea7000c:
You feel like this man might know something else, and your hunch is right. The moment you fall silent, he leans in and whispers conspiratorially.
— There is some kind of evil spirit in our well. Along with the water you get strange prophecies. Everyone sees their own version.
es.687446ca5dadd51c3ab2e0a1: From his reaction you can tell he will not say anything more, at least nothing useful. You missed your chance by not buying anything.
