You turn to the ghost. Suddenly, you realize something.
ro.68776b9d6a7c1975fec78b1e:
You freeze in place, staring at the ghost. She tilts her head slightly and leans toward you.
— Good thing you didn’t run.
Her voice echoes somewhere in your head. You don’t look away.
— You are on my territory anyway.
Suddenly, you realize something.
ro.68776bab64c7af8a31e15fc3:
But your words pass the ghost by. You see frost tracing paths from her body toward you. The woman’s ghost roars and lunges at you. In a second, her semi-transparent hand plunges into your chest.
You expect pain, but a second passes, then another... and nothing happens. The ghost recoils and hovers again over the body.
ro.68776be609bb97fe9897d4c4:
The ghost smiles, and a wave of anxiety hits you. Why is she smiling? Her attack didn't work! You are alive and…
Suddenly, pain pierces your chest. You stagger. The pain radiates to your back and arm. The ghost’s smile widens.
— What about now? Do you like it?
You hear her otherworldly voice as you fall to your knees. Breathing is now impossible. You barely understand what happened before consciousness leaves you.
As does your life.
ro.68776bf436f95980e2f53933: Is it your doing that I can’t get out of the swamps?
ro.68776c7650ab4fd648bdcecc:
The ghostly girl nods.
— You won’t leave here until I allow it.
And you realize she is not lying. But why does she need all this?
ro.68776c815950c83fded8767a:
— Help me, and I will let you go, — the ghost flickers between clarity and a ripple, like a lake disturbed by a thrown stone.
You involuntarily glance at the body lying beneath her.
ro.68776c901d977782c497b92d: "It doesn’t look like I can help you with anything."
ro.68776c9fc271e98e8ef3d76a: — I mean myself! Not the body. — the ghost shifts for a moment. You flinch as a bloodthirsty snarl flashes across her face, but a second later, her expression is calm again. It seems she dislikes useless questions. Best remember that.

ru.687766ebf0699320ec0fe4fa:
Наконец-то ты оказался на другой стороне реки. Ты оглядываешься назад, на переправу. Никто тебя не провожает и это даже хорошо. Не хватало ещё раз посмотреть на лица этих разбойников.
Ты всё ещё не понимаешь, откуда узнал пароль. Наверняка это Господь благословил тебя тайным знанием. Значит, он хочет, чтобы ты добрался до Тарграда. Значит, твоя работа важна. Это понимание подталкивает тебя вперёд.
ru.6877670b53d4a9a319899bf6: Впереди раскинулись болота. Солнце прячется за облаками всё чаще. Ты идёшь вперед, ступая легко. Наверняка все трудности уже позади. До Тарграда осталось совсем немного.
ru.6877670d8eed8b191d44bac1: Впереди раскинулись болота. Солнце прячется за облаками всё чаще. Ты идёшь вперед, чуть хмурясь. Все твои ссадины болят, поэтому ты двигаешься куда медленее, чем планировал. Наверняка все трудности уже позади. До Тарграда осталось совсем немного.
ru.6877684bf5462f66938541ce: Ты идёшь и идёшь вперед. Болота вокруг так похожи друг на друга, что ты перестаёшь понимать, где ты именно. Проходит полчаса. Проходит час. Ты смотришь на карту и понимаешь, что должен был выйти на сухую и твёрдую землю, но болота не кончаются.
ru.6877687f997e504b36dcdf95: Ты вздыхаешь и продолжаешь двигаться. Может быть, карта неточная, может быть, ты сбился с пути. Но рано или поздно ты куда-нибудь выйдешь, если не будешь сходить с дороги. Выйдешь же?..
ru.68776882bbe160d53138531b:
Ты останавливаешься и смотришь по сторонам. Наверное, ты где-то свернул не туда. Надо вернуться назад и начать всё заново. Ты разворачиваешься и идёшь прочь.
Только вот ты не видишь заставы ни через полчаса, ни через час. Тревога поднимается внутри тебя. Что за чертовщина происходит?
ru.6877688f2d23e8bc3a1393c4:
Наконец, ты видишь перед собой избушку и останавливаешься. Вокруг сплошные непроходимые болота, как кто-то смог выжить тут в одиночку?
Домик выглядит ухоженным, но каким-то... потусторонним.
ru.68776942b4647b668bb233ef:
Дом, конечно, милый и такой загадочный, но тебе сейчас нет смысла лезть не в своё дело. Тебе нужно добраться до Тарграда как можно скорее.
Ты проходишь мимо дома и возвращаешься на дорогу.
ru.6877694b344a9779e0e4eebe:
Ты идёшь. И идёшь. И идёшь.
Дорогая тянется вперед узкой лентой, петляет среди болотных кочек. Ты видишь впереди какое-то строение, подходишь ближе...
ru.6877695906bf1da56f74700d:
...и понимаешь, что перед тобой тот самый дом. Ты даже подошёл к нему с той же стороны, что и в прошлый раз. Неужели ты заблудился? Но ты помнишь, что шёл по абсолютно прямой дороге!
Здесь точно замешана магия. И её хозяин хочет, чтобы ты зашёл в дом.
ru.687769673ee96886e458b3eb:
Дверь в дом просто прикрыта. Ты толкаешь её и делаешь шаг внутрь.
Первым делом ты замечаешь лежащий почти на самом пороге труп. Потом — развешанные под самым потолком сушеные травы. Ты понимаешь, что здесь живёт какая-то ведьма. Ты опускаешь взгляд на труп. Или жила.
ru.687769a706b143c57b8037cd: Да пошло оно всё! Я ухожу.
ru.687769d09aa1bbe99a33f796:
Ты собираешься уйти и продолжить скитаться по болотам в поиске выхода, как неожиданно какая-то сила тянет тебя обратно.
"Помоги..."
Ты вздрагиваешь и смотришь по сторонам. Шёпот, ты точно его слышал! Но ведь рядом никого нет, только... Ты смотришь на труп. Мурашки бегут по спине. Кажется, кто-то — или что-то — не хочет тебя отпускать просто так. У тебя просто нет выбора.
ru.687769f769b0ec97a0682d05:
Ты проходишь дальше. Избушка явно рассчитана на одного человека: ты находишь только одну кровать, один набор деревянной посуды. Всё здесь пропитано магией и неожиданно домашним уютом. Нет ни странных котлов с подозрительным варевом, ни дьявольских меток, ни чёрных кошек или петухов. Если бы этот домик не стоял посреди болот на пнях, то ты никогда бы не отличил его от любой деревенской хаты.
Ты не находишь ничего интересного.
ru.68776a1371aceff1114f9edf: Ты подходишь ближе и встаёшь прямо над телом. Девушка лежит ничком, из её спины торчит меч. Вряд ли кто-то добровольно оставил своё оружие в трупе. Ты рассматриваешь меч и понимаешь, что стоит он немало.
ru.68776a53f94c9d419ec4b9d4: Ты подходишь ближе и хватаешься за рукоять меча. Неожиданно твои ладони обжигает таким холодом, какой ты никогда не ощущал. Ты рефлекторно одёргиваешь руки.
ru.68776a6fcc97fe1f9012c020: Ты решаешь оставить меч на своём месте. Что-то внутри тебя сопротивляется идее калечить тело незнакомки ещё сильнее. Наверное, стоит вообще перенести её и похоронить во дворе.
ru.68776a896c8e2be82eb23fd7: Но не успеваешь ты наклониться, как из тела прямо перед тобой появляется призрак. Ты отшатываешься назад, не зная, что делать.
ru.68776aa6b1d9b19c4f986bbc:
Ты не считываешь предупреждение. Впереди у тебя путь до Тарграда. Наверняка разбойники с переправы не единственные, кто воспользовался слабостью города. Меч тебе нужнее, чем хладному телу.
Ты снова хватаешься за рукоять, стискивая зубы от холода, и тянешь меч на себя. Он выскальзывает из тела.
ru.68776ab0ae2b125a0898bbfc:
Неожиданно тебя откидывает от тела волной силы. Ты ударяешься о стену и переводишь дух. Прямо перед тобой из мёртвого тела поднимается призрак убитой. В избушке холодает так сильно, что тебя начинает бить озноб. Или это от страха?
Лицо призрака искажено в ярости.
— Как ты смеешь издеваться над телом невинной жертвы?!
ru.68776b4b13febab7d8bdc1cc: Призрак смеётся. Её смех разносится по всей избушке, а по твоей спине бегут мурашки. Что же тебе делать?
ru.68776b50260dd115ac338e51:
Призрак не отвечает тебе, только улыбается. Ты видишь перед собой не труп, а молодую девушку. Но не стоит обольщаться, напоминаешь ты себе, нечисть остаётся нечистью.
Что же тебе делать?
ru.68776b9b9831684f832bba27:
Ты решаешь рискнуть. Выход из избушки совсем рядом, ты успеешь добраться до него.
Ты вскакиваешь на ноги и бросаешься к распахнутой двери.
Хлопок — и дверь закрывается прямо перед тобой. Ты дёргаешь ручку, но без результата.
— Не надо убегать. Всё равно не получится. Ты на моей территории.
Ты оборачиваешься на призрак. Неожиданно ты кое-что понимаешь.
ru.68776b9d6a7c1975fec78b1e:
Ты замираешь на месте и просто смотришь на призрака. Она чуть склоняет голову и подаётся к тебе.
— Хорошо, что не побежал.
Её голос отдаётся эхом где-то у тебя в голове. Ты не сводишь с неё взгляда.
— Всё равно ты на моей территории.
Неожиданно ты кое-что понимаешь.
ru.68776bab64c7af8a31e15fc3:
Но твои слова проходят мимо призрака. Ты видишь, как от тела бегут дорожки инея в твою сторону. Призрак женщины ревёт и бросается в твою сторону. Секунда — и её полупрозрачная рука погружается тебе в грудь.
Ты ждёшь боли, но проходит секунда, другая и ничего не происходит. Призрак отшатывается назад и снова зависает над телом.
ru.68776be609bb97fe9897d4c4:
Призрак улыбается, тревога захлёстывает тебя. Почему она улыбается? Ничего же не сработало! Ты живой и...
Неожиданно боль пронзает твою грудь. Ты пошатываешься. Боль отдаётся в спину и руку. Улыбка призрака становится шире.
— А сейчас? Нравится?
Ты слышишь её потусторонний голос, падая на колени. Сделать вдох сейчас — непосильная задача. Ты толком не успеваешь понять что произошло, когда сознание покидает тебя.
Как и жизнь.
ru.68776bf436f95980e2f53933: То, что я не могу выбраться с болот — твоих рук дело?
ru.68776c7650ab4fd648bdcecc:
Призрачная девушка кивает.
— Ты не сможешь выбраться отсюда, пока я не разрешу.
И ты понимаешь, что она не врёт. Только вот зачем ей это всё?
ru.68776c815950c83fded8767a:
— Помоги мне, и я выпущу тебя, — призрак то становится чуть чётче, то наоборот идёт рябью, словно озеро, куда кинули камень.
Ты невольно смотришь на тело, лежащее под призраком.
ru.68776c901d977782c497b92d: Не похоже, что я могу чем-то тебе помочь.
ru.68776c9fc271e98e8ef3d76a: — Я про себя! А не про тело. — призрак на секунду меняется. Ты вздрагиваешь, когда на её лице мелькает кровожадный оскал нечисти, но через секунду лицо снова становится спокойным. Кажется, ей не нравятся вопросы ни о чём. Стоит это запомнить.

sk.687766ebf0699320ec0fe4fa:
Finally, you reach the other side of the river. You look back at the crossing. No one is seeing you off, and that’s for the best. The last thing you want is to see the faces of those bandits again.
You still don’t understand how you knew the password. Surely it was the Lord who blessed you with secret knowledge. That means He wants you to reach Targrad. That means your work is important. This understanding pushes you forward.
sk.6877670b53d4a9a319899bf6: Ahead, the swamps stretch out. The sun hides behind clouds more and more often. You walk forward, stepping lightly. Surely all the difficulties are behind you. Targrad is not far now.
sk.6877670d8eed8b191d44bac1: Ahead, the swamps stretch out. The sun hides behind clouds more and more often. You walk forward, frowning slightly. All your scratches hurt, so you move slower than planned. But it’s fine: surely all the difficulties are behind you. Targrad is not far now.
sk.6877684bf5462f66938541ce: You walk and walk. The swamps around look so alike that you stop knowing exactly where you are. Half an hour passes. An hour passes. You look at the map and realize you should have reached solid, dry land, but the swamps don’t end.
sk.6877687f997e504b36dcdf95: You sigh and keep moving. Maybe the map is inaccurate, maybe you lost your way. But sooner or later, you’ll reach somewhere if you stay on the path. Right?..
sk.68776882bbe160d53138531b:
You stop and look around. Surely you turned the wrong way somewhere. You need to go back and start over. You turn around and head away.
But you don’t see the outpost after half an hour, nor after an hour. Anxiety rises inside you. What the hell is going on?
sk.6877688f2d23e8bc3a1393c4:
Finally, you see a hut ahead and stop. Impassable swamps surround it. How could anyone survive here alone?
The house looks well-kept, but somehow... otherworldly.
sk.68776942b4647b668bb233ef:
The house is cute and mysterious, but now is not the time to meddle in things that aren’t yours. You need to reach Targrad as soon as possible.
You pass the house and continue onward.
sk.6877694b344a9779e0e4eebe:
You walk. And walk. And walk.
The road stretches ahead like a narrow ribbon, winding among swampy hummocks. You see a structure ahead and approach…
sk.6877695906bf1da56f74700d:
...and realize that it is the same house. You even approached it from the same side as last time. Could you have gotten lost? But you remember walking on an absolutely straight road!
This is definitely some kind of magic. And its owner wants you to enter the house.
sk.687769673ee96886e458b3eb:
The door is slightly open. You push it and step inside.
The first thing you notice is a body lying almost on the threshold. Beyond it are herbs hanging from the ceiling. You realize some witch lives here. You lower your gaze to the body. Or, rather, lived here.
sk.687769a706b143c57b8037cd: To hell with it! Time to leave.
sk.687769b96724922b7c3a977d: Better examine the house more carefully.
sk.687769d09aa1bbe99a33f796:
You are about to leave and continue wandering the swamps in search of an exit, when suddenly some force pulls you back.
"Help me..."
You shiver and look around. A whisper, you definitely heard it! But there’s no one around, only… You look at the body. Goosebumps run down your spine. It seems someone — or something — doesn’t want to let you go easily. You simply have no choice.
sk.687769e87fd67688da56cfc1: Better examine the house more carefully.
sk.687769f769b0ec97a0682d05:
You move further. The hut is clearly meant for one person: you find only one bed, one set of wooden dishes. Everything here is imbued with magic and unexpectedly homely comfort. No strange cauldrons with suspicious brews, no devilish marks, no black cats or roosters. If this hut weren’t standing on swamp stumps, you would never distinguish it from any regular village house.
You find nothing interesting.
sk.68776a1371aceff1114f9edf: You approach and stand directly over the corpse. A young woman lies face down, a sword protruding from her back. No one would voluntarily leave their weapon in a corpse. You look at the sword and realize it’s quite expensive.
sk.68776a53f94c9d419ec4b9d4: You approach and grab the sword’s hilt. Suddenly, your palms are burned by a cold like nothing you’ve ever felt. Reflexively, you pull your hands back.
sk.68776a5e2319985d4d57c354: Perhaps it's better not try this again.
sk.68776a6fcc97fe1f9012c020: You decide to leave the sword in place. Something inside you resists the idea of further mutilating the body of a stranger. Perhaps you should even move her and bury her in the yard.
sk.68776a896c8e2be82eb23fd7: But before you can bend down, a ghost rises from the body right before you. You recoil, unsure what to do.
sk.68776aa6b1d9b19c4f986bbc:
You ignore the warning. Ahead lies the path to Targrad. Surely the bandits from the crossing are not the only ones who exploited the city’s weakness. You need the sword more than the cold corpse.
You grab the hilt again, clenching your teeth against the cold, and pull the sword out. It slides from the body.
sk.68776ab0ae2b125a0898bbfc:
Suddenly, a wave of force throws you back. You hit the wall and catch your breath. Before you, the ghost of the murdered woman rises. The hut grows so cold that you start shivering. Or is it fear?
The ghost’s face is twisted in rage.
—How dare you mock the body of an innocent victim?!
sk.68776b3da3fae9cbf8be4b29: "Don’t come near, you ghoulish specter! You creature!"
sk.68776b4b13febab7d8bdc1cc: The ghost laughs. Her laughter echoes through the hut, sending chills down your spine. What do you do?
sk.68776b50260dd115ac338e51:
The ghost does not answer, only smiles. You see not a corpse, but a young woman. But don’t be deceived, you remind yourself, evil spirit remains evil spirit.
What do you do?
sk.68776b9b9831684f832bba27:
You decide to take a risk. The hut’s exit is very close, you can make it.
You jump to your feet and rush for the open door.
Bang — the door closes right in front of you. You tug the handle, but it doesn’t budge.
— Do not run. You won’t succeed anyway. You are on my territory.
You turn to the ghost. Suddenly, you realize something.
sk.68776b9d6a7c1975fec78b1e:
You freeze in place, staring at the ghost. She tilts her head slightly and leans toward you.
— Good thing you didn’t run.
Her voice echoes somewhere in your head. You don’t look away.
— You are on my territory anyway.
Suddenly, you realize something.
sk.68776bab64c7af8a31e15fc3:
But your words pass the ghost by. You see frost tracing paths from her body toward you. The woman’s ghost roars and lunges at you. In a second, her semi-transparent hand plunges into your chest.
You expect pain, but a second passes, then another... and nothing happens. The ghost recoils and hovers again over the body.
sk.68776be609bb97fe9897d4c4:
The ghost smiles, and a wave of anxiety hits you. Why is she smiling? Her attack didn't work! You are alive and…
Suddenly, pain pierces your chest. You stagger. The pain radiates to your back and arm. The ghost’s smile widens.
— What about now? Do you like it?
You hear her otherworldly voice as you fall to your knees. Breathing is now impossible. You barely understand what happened before consciousness leaves you.
As does your life.
sk.68776bf436f95980e2f53933: Is it your doing that I can’t get out of the swamps?
sk.68776c7650ab4fd648bdcecc:
The ghostly girl nods.
— You won’t leave here until I allow it.
And you realize she is not lying. But why does she need all this?
sk.68776c815950c83fded8767a:
— Help me, and I will let you go, — the ghost flickers between clarity and a ripple, like a lake disturbed by a thrown stone.
You involuntarily glance at the body lying beneath her.
sk.68776c901d977782c497b92d: "It doesn’t look like I can help you with anything."
sk.68776c9fc271e98e8ef3d76a: — I mean myself! Not the body. — the ghost shifts for a moment. You flinch as a bloodthirsty snarl flashes across her face, but a second later, her expression is calm again. It seems she dislikes useless questions. Best remember that.

tu.6877694b344a9779e0e4eebe:
You walk. And walk. And walk.
The road stretches ahead like a narrow ribbon, winding among swampy hummocks. You see a structure ahead and approach…
tu.6877695906bf1da56f74700d:
...and realize that it is the same house. You even approached it from the same side as last time. Could you have gotten lost? But you remember walking on an absolutely straight road!
This is definitely some kind of magic. And its owner wants you to enter the house.
tu.687769673ee96886e458b3eb:
The door is slightly open. You push it and step inside.
The first thing you notice is a body lying almost on the threshold. Beyond it are herbs hanging from the ceiling. You realize some witch lives here. You lower your gaze to the body. Or, rather, lived here.
tu.687769a706b143c57b8037cd: To hell with it! Time to leave.
tu.687769b96724922b7c3a977d: Better examine the house more carefully.
tu.687769d09aa1bbe99a33f796:
You are about to leave and continue wandering the swamps in search of an exit, when suddenly some force pulls you back.
"Help me..."
You shiver and look around. A whisper, you definitely heard it! But there’s no one around, only… You look at the body. Goosebumps run down your spine. It seems someone — or something — doesn’t want to let you go easily. You simply have no choice.
tu.687769e87fd67688da56cfc1: Better examine the house more carefully.
tu.687769f769b0ec97a0682d05:
You move further. The hut is clearly meant for one person: you find only one bed, one set of wooden dishes. Everything here is imbued with magic and unexpectedly homely comfort. No strange cauldrons with suspicious brews, no devilish marks, no black cats or roosters. If this hut weren’t standing on swamp stumps, you would never distinguish it from any regular village house.
You find nothing interesting.
tu.68776a1371aceff1114f9edf: You approach and stand directly over the corpse. A young woman lies face down, a sword protruding from her back. No one would voluntarily leave their weapon in a corpse. You look at the sword and realize it’s quite expensive.
tu.68776a53f94c9d419ec4b9d4: You approach and grab the sword’s hilt. Suddenly, your palms are burned by a cold like nothing you’ve ever felt. Reflexively, you pull your hands back.
tu.68776a5e2319985d4d57c354: Perhaps it's better not try this again.
tu.68776a6fcc97fe1f9012c020: You decide to leave the sword in place. Something inside you resists the idea of further mutilating the body of a stranger. Perhaps you should even move her and bury her in the yard.
tu.68776a896c8e2be82eb23fd7: But before you can bend down, a ghost rises from the body right before you. You recoil, unsure what to do.
tu.68776aa6b1d9b19c4f986bbc:
You ignore the warning. Ahead lies the path to Targrad. Surely the bandits from the crossing are not the only ones who exploited the city’s weakness. You need the sword more than the cold corpse.
You grab the hilt again, clenching your teeth against the cold, and pull the sword out. It slides from the body.
tu.68776ab0ae2b125a0898bbfc:
Suddenly, a wave of force throws you back. You hit the wall and catch your breath. Before you, the ghost of the murdered woman rises. The hut grows so cold that you start shivering. Or is it fear?
The ghost’s face is twisted in rage.
—How dare you mock the body of an innocent victim?!
tu.68776b3da3fae9cbf8be4b29: "Don’t come near, you ghoulish specter! You creature!"
tu.68776b4b13febab7d8bdc1cc: The ghost laughs. Her laughter echoes through the hut, sending chills down your spine. What do you do?
tu.68776b50260dd115ac338e51:
The ghost does not answer, only smiles. You see not a corpse, but a young woman. But don’t be deceived, you remind yourself, evil spirit remains evil spirit.
What do you do?
tu.68776b9b9831684f832bba27:
You decide to take a risk. The hut’s exit is very close, you can make it.
You jump to your feet and rush for the open door.
Bang — the door closes right in front of you. You tug the handle, but it doesn’t budge.
— Do not run. You won’t succeed anyway. You are on my territory.
You turn to the ghost. Suddenly, you realize something.
tu.68776b9d6a7c1975fec78b1e:
You freeze in place, staring at the ghost. She tilts her head slightly and leans toward you.
— Good thing you didn’t run.
Her voice echoes somewhere in your head. You don’t look away.
— You are on my territory anyway.
Suddenly, you realize something.
tu.68776bab64c7af8a31e15fc3:
But your words pass the ghost by. You see frost tracing paths from her body toward you. The woman’s ghost roars and lunges at you. In a second, her semi-transparent hand plunges into your chest.
You expect pain, but a second passes, then another... and nothing happens. The ghost recoils and hovers again over the body.
tu.68776be609bb97fe9897d4c4:
The ghost smiles, and a wave of anxiety hits you. Why is she smiling? Her attack didn't work! You are alive and…
Suddenly, pain pierces your chest. You stagger. The pain radiates to your back and arm. The ghost’s smile widens.
— What about now? Do you like it?
You hear her otherworldly voice as you fall to your knees. Breathing is now impossible. You barely understand what happened before consciousness leaves you.
As does your life.
tu.68776bf436f95980e2f53933: Is it your doing that I can’t get out of the swamps?
tu.68776c7650ab4fd648bdcecc:
The ghostly girl nods.
— You won’t leave here until I allow it.
And you realize she is not lying. But why does she need all this?
tu.68776c815950c83fded8767a:
— Help me, and I will let you go, — the ghost flickers between clarity and a ripple, like a lake disturbed by a thrown stone.
You involuntarily glance at the body lying beneath her.
tu.68776c901d977782c497b92d: "It doesn’t look like I can help you with anything."
tu.68776c9fc271e98e8ef3d76a: — I mean myself! Not the body. — the ghost shifts for a moment. You flinch as a bloodthirsty snarl flashes across her face, but a second later, her expression is calm again. It seems she dislikes useless questions. Best remember that.

ch.68776e51a583a513398d76fe:
— My murderers must face punishment. But first, you must return what they stole from me.
You don’t know how to respond. It’s like everything’s already been decided for you. But maybe you should try something...
ch.68776f130a3d5213d0b5b8aa:
The ghost leans forward, stopping mere inches from your face. Her voice turns into an eerie, otherworldly hiss.
— I don’t care. You’re here, so you’ll manage, — she says, pulling back with a careless shrug. — You don’t need to be a warrior. Being a thief will do.
ch.68776f27279785c6efb5aa5f:
— They came from the village by the road. Their home is there, and so is my stolen mirror. Bring it back to me.
You nod resignedly. The ghost glides beside you, placing her hand on your cheek. Or she would have, if she were alive. Instead, you feel an unbearable cold. Your cheek goes numb, but you stand still, unmoving. The witch pulls away and gestures toward the sword protruding from her body.
— Take this sword. You might need it. Now go, and don’t fail me.
ch.68776f9e898fc18e5b451dc3:
You step out of the hut and exhale shakily. A gentle breeze warms your chilled body. Rubbing your cheeks with your hands, you shrug off the lingering cold and adjust the bag on your shoulder. Now, a sword rests inside it.
You still haven’t fully processed what happened. Did you ever think you’d meet a ghost? Or help one?
But you have no choice. The witch’s magic won’t let you leave the swamps. You must do as she asked.
ch.68776fb1e03472f2f9d57bd9:
You head toward the village. This time, you don’t wander and walk straight to it.
At first, you don’t realize what’s wrong, but then the sparse swamp trees part, revealing the full scene.
The village is burned and pillaged. You freeze in place.
ch.68776fc7ac55d85e4e94c8a2: The wind carries the suffocating stench of smoke and burned flesh. You see corpses, such devastation... You want to flee, but your task holds you here. You must reach Targrad, no matter the cost. Perhaps the witch’s murderers are already dead... If so, bringing her the artifact might be enough. You hope it will satisfy her.
ch.68776fcafea5ef3f947f96d0:
The witch said her murderers were holed up in this village. But what do you do if they’re all dead now? Will the ghost listen to you? Or will she think you’re trying to deceive her?  
You realize you’re in deep trouble. But maybe you can at least find the artifact?
ch.68776fe61d62f818144929b3:
You approach the edge of the ruined village, crouching and moving cautiously. Whoever destroyed this place couldn’t have gotten far. The witch’s curse wouldn’t allow it.
Suddenly, you hear voices. They’re not begging for help or mourning the dead; they’re discussing mundane things. You realize these are the ones who attacked the village.
ch.687770119a6b54bdde1a5e09: Well, you’ve got nothing to lose. If they’re trapped here like you, maybe they won’t attack right away. If they do, death might spare you from carrying out the witch’s errand.
ch.6877701680ac1c8fc0a67cf8:
You decide to stay hidden for now. Who knows what these men, capable of destroying an entire village, might do to you? Luckily, none of them notice you.
You press yourself against the corner of a burned-out house and listen.
One man has a deep voice with a slight, unfamiliar accent. The other speaks without an accent, his voice higher and almost shrill.
— How can a village like this have so few supplies? I’m starving, and there’s nothing, — grumbles the one with the accent.
— We’re gonna die here! These swamps are cursed, and we’ve got no idea how to break the spell, — the shrill one replies hysterically. You realize they’re trapped here by the curse too. And they’re hungry.
ch.687770255d653efcf402554c:
You step forward, raising your hands to show you come in peace. Several tired-looking men stand before you. They grip their weapons tighter, eyeing you with wary fear as you emerge from behind the half-burned house.
— A live one, — says one of the men, slightly relaxing his shoulders. — Who are you?
You hear a faint accent in his voice, but you can’t place it. Not that it matters right now.
ch.68777038f3c351577685307e:
— I swear, chief knows something. Like, why we’re stuck here, — the shrill one lowers his voice, forcing you to lean forward to hear.
— Cut it out. How would he know? — The one with the accent seems less suspicious. — Don’t badmouth our leader!
— Alright, alright, it's just a theory!
You hear their footsteps fade as the men walk away.
ch.68777068417fdab26ffb8723:
You think the men might reveal more useful information. You follow them as quietly as possible, straining to listen, but you get too caught up and step on a dry, heat-cracked branch. It snaps loudly, and the men hear it.
— Who’s there? Come out now!
ch.687770798620a3432a97173b: Step out from your hiding spot.
ch.68777097aef5de13e6265bc8:
You can’t think of anything better than to bolt. You dart around the corner. The house you were hiding behind is missing a wall, so the men spot you.
— Stop, you little rat! — the shrill one yells. You notice him giving chase. The other man, for some reason, is nowhere in sight.
ch.687770ab8a0d6fb48d25b5cb: But not for long. He suddenly appears in front of you, stepping out from around a corner. You veer to the side, but there’s a pile of half-burned logs blocking your path. Behind you, the shrill one is closing in. You’re trapped.
ch.687770bdc888ca05f005a144: "I’m a messenger of the Order of Navigators!"
ch.687770c4d13a96e750824979:
— Then why were you eavesdropping? — the one with the accent asks, still skeptical, though he lowers his sword.
— Yeah, and why’d you run? — the shrill one chimes in.
ch.687770c82e35b771f834f773: — We’ve never heard of that, — the accented one says, drawing his sword again and eyeing you suspiciously. You’ve got one last card to play.
ch.6877710b743696531c94767d:
The men exchange glances and burst into synchronized laughter.
— What’s so funny? — a new voice booms, low and harsh. Both men snap to attention. You turn around.
From behind the ruins of another burned house, several more figures emerge. They’re clearly from the same band: exhausted, angry, and deeply terrified beneath it all.
— Who’s this now? — a tall man in leather armor stares at you. His mustache is sharply twisted, and his gaze drips with disdain and distrust.
Well, it seems this is the leader. You’re already exhausted from dealing with bandits today!
ch.68777142b10562bdb441afbc: "I’m just a messenger of the Order of Navigators."
ch.687771498198fb94b7c7f178:
The men exchange glances at your words.
— Never heard of it. Where’d you come from? All the locals are long dead.
They tense up again and start closing in on you.
ch.6877714dcd7817d80cab402c:
Now the men look at you differently.
— We’ve been trying to get out of here for who knows how long! — says one who’d been silent until now. The other elbows him in the side.
— Just spill everything already!
— What’s it matter? Maybe he’s been sent to sort this mess and get us out!
ch.68777164c6503bbfbef44368: "I know something... Maybe I can help."
ch.68777172ecaff18af8343399:
You realize this is your chance, there won’t be another. The men stare at you, as if weighing your words. Something you said clearly struck a chord.
Suddenly, there’s a noise nearby. From behind the ruins of another burned house, several more figures emerge. They’re clearly part of the same band: exhausted, angry, and deeply terrified beneath it all.
— Who’s this now? — a tall man in leather armor stares at you. His mustache is sharply twisted, and his gaze drips with disdain and distrust. Your new acquaintances both snap to attention.
Well, it seems this is the leader. You’re already exhausted from dealing with bandits today!
ch.6877717c1c47f3efb21336d5:
— He says he’s trapped here like us. Says he might help, — one of them introduces you. The leader squints and sneers.
— And how’s this runt supposed to help us? Can you even hold a sword?
ch.687771b646f9b37bd9a181fb: "I know what will get us all out of here."
ch.687771bd405ba3f4e15b922c:
The bandit leader raises an eyebrow, then laughs with a cruel, mocking sound. His lackeys join in, their laughter hollow.
— In what, then? Writing? We don’t need scribes. Words? Those are useless too.
ch.687771c1612fd19c7a89c97d: "I know what will get us all out of here."
ch.687771cda360c1de351bf14a:
You see the entire group staring at you, hope flickering in their eyes. The leader, though, isn’t convinced.
— Why should we trust you? Tell us what you know first, then we’ll decide if you’re worth believing.
ch.687771f65c6bc4cd5a76e726:
You decide there’s no point in hiding anything. These bandits want to escape the cursed swamps just as badly as you do. Right now, you’re allies, and many of them likely understand that.
— It’s all because of the locals. They killed the swamp witch and stole a valuable artifact. She wants it back. And, of course, she wants revenge.
A few bandits glance around nervously, as if looking for those responsible for the witch’s death. But alas, they’re the ones who killed them.
ch.687771fb4af817d6da36adb1:
These are the bandits who wiped out an entire village. Trusting them completely would be foolish. What if they kill you as soon as they hear the truth? You decide to play it safe.
— t’s because of the witch. She was killed and robbed by the people of this village. She sent me to find what was stolen. If anything happens to me, she’ll destroy everyone in the area.
Of course, the witch never said you were particularly important, but the bandits don’t need to know that.
You see in their eyes that they believe you. Now they look at you with more respect than before. Some even step back slightly, as if afraid.
ch.68777209d2f6c5d9902e84b5: — So, what do you suggest we do? — the leader asks, frowning and staring at you expectantly.
ch.6877724575c61507df6aa339: "We need to find the stolen mirror."
ch.68777248a82ae5340e85a3b4: "We need to figure out how to trick the witch."
ch.6877725b6e4d07907a24ec43:
Why come up with something new when the witch already gave you a clear path? Sure, you can’t punish the guilty, but maybe that’s for the best?
The bandit leader frowns discontentedly. Something shifts in his movements, but you can’t quite place what. You’re distracted by the high-pitched voice of a young man standing just behind him.  
— We did see a strange mirror that doesn’t burn! A round one.
The leader spins toward the young man and practically growls:
— That’s definitely. Not. It!
You freeze, as does the young man. That kind of reaction can only mean one thing.
ch.6877725ec0232b786f36d303:
You realize the witch probably won’t be satisfied with just the artifact. And that’s not even considering how you’ll get it in the first place. You start to think, but the same young man who mentioned the mirror suddenly speaks up again.
— What if we just banish the witch? — everyone turns to look at him, and he shrugs, — I would’ve tried earlier, but we didn’t know about the witch!
ch.68777ec7e80e2cdbbbf16d59: "Do you know how to do that?"
ch.68777ecb09285caee7e293ed: "Is there anyone here who knows how to do that?"
ch.68777eea8cf0f973aecd50a8:
— Well, yeah, I know how, — the young man says, puffing out his chest with a boastful grin. — I was a priest with Turva’s band. I’ve done crazier things than this!
It’s a reasonable idea. But can you really trust your life to some young kid?
ch.68777eed0334393e733d8657:
— Yeah, I do, — the young man says, spreading his arms, — I was a priest with Turva’s band. I’ve done crazier things than this.
It’s a solid idea. But can you really trust your life to some kid?
ch.68777f1371ec3fda827cd7a4: You shake your head. Maybe the kid really is a priest, but taking such a risk... You want to escape these swamps, not get stuck here forever because of an angry witch’s whim.
ch.68777f1a90768808625407d6:
Here goes nothing! You agree to the young man’s plan. The leader rubs his chin thoughtfully, then shrugs:
— Might as well try. We’ve got nothing to lose.
He turns his gaze to you.
— Alright, lead the way to where this witch of yours is hiding.
ch.68777f632cb5f630737f0645: "We need to find the stolen mirror."
ch.68777fdde9dbf46430a8b89a:
You lead the group through the swamps, heading straight for the hut. The journey seems to take longer than it should, but you brush off the strangeness.
You stop right in front of the hut. The young man who claims to be a priest tugs at your sleeve to get your attention.
— By the way, I’m Mstislav. Call me Slavka, — he says with a grin, nodding toward the hut. — Just thought you should know the name of the guy who’s gonna banish that witch, right?
He laughs, as if he’s not scared at all.
ch.68777ff59f3cf8c68c46e6a3:
The leader turns to you, glaring with disdain.
— And if I’ve got the mirror, so what? You gonna take it from me? Think you're up for it?
ch.68778003999b2330c41b3ccb:
Your body aches from what happened just hours ago. You draw your sword, but your movements are clumsy. The bandit leader smirks, watching your struggle with the weapon.
— You’ve never held anything heavier than a quill, you little punk!
He deftly draws his own sword and advances, winding up for a strike. You realize the force of his blow will be too much for you to block.
ch.6877800552157c87b8a740c7:
You surprisingly draw your sword with ease. Traces of the witch’s blood still stain the blade, but you pay it no mind. You have a goal, and nothing stands in your way. You grip the hilt tightly and lock eyes with the leader.
— Look at this serious guy! — they mock, but you don’t take the bait.
The leader draws his weapon and comes at you, winding up for a strike.
ch.6877809c1f2529646b28b4de:
You slide to the side, dodging the path of the strike. The sword whistles past your ear but doesn’t touch you. The leader spins with the momentum, trying to hit you again. You leap back.
The other bandits haven’t joined the fight yet. You see confusion on their faces. It’s dawning on them that their leader is willing to sacrifice both his life and theirs for greed.
You realize you could call out to them. But doing so might distract you, leaving you open to the leader’s next strike.
ch.6877809f9322bd17f049d9e6: ...But what does it matter? The fury of battle engulfs you, its fire burning hot. You meet the leader’s strike with your blade... or try to, as the force of his blow obliterates your barely prepared defense. You’re knocked to the side, tripping over a charred piece of wood and falling. You don’t scream, no, just curse and struggle to get up.
ch.687780e458982e675f3b55ec:
The leader steps closer and spits near you. For a moment, you freeze, looking up at him.
— Too much pride, you little punk, — he sneers, raising his sword above you, — Send my regards to that witch of yours.
He swings down. The blade cuts through your unarmored body like butter, slicing your heart.
You die before you can take your final breath.
ch.687780f9863b6ec75207f1a5: "Don’t you see he’s ready to risk your lives for his own gain?!"
ch.68778108bc8407c6acdf1e18:
You notice a few bandits flinch, exchanging glances. You know standing up alone against someone stronger is always terrifying, but there are so many of them! You hope for their common sense.  
And you’re not wrong.
The young man who mentioned the mirror is the first to raise his hand.
— He’s really ready to cling to that mirror until he dies!
Another man nods, grabbing his battle axe.
— Yeah, until we all die here like dogs! How many days have we been slogging through these swamps?! My junk’s already crawling with leeches!
One by one, they start grumbling angrily. You’d love to listen, but the leader clearly plans to deal with you first before sorting out the others.
ch.6877810c4dcbc02930d301bc:
There’s no time to get distracted. Dying a martyr to some pathetic deserter bandit’s blade isn’t the fate you dreamed of.

You miss the chance to gain allies but don’t miss the leader’s strike. Dodging just in time, you swing back, but he deftly parries and nicks you with his sword. The blade tears through your clothes and slices your side. You scream in pain.

— Not so brave now, huh? — the leader taunts, stepping closer. His eyes gleam with bloodlust.

Suddenly, you feel a presence, something intangible to ordinary senses. The air grows colder, and you shiver. Something is trying to merge with you. You hear a faint whisper: "Let me in".
ch.68778175a6d0eaf0f969dd89:
You’ve felt this cold before, back in the swamp hut. The witch has come to your aid, and who are you to refuse her?
You let her in, gasping from the icy chill. It feels like being plunged into a frozen lake in winter.
From that moment, you’re a passenger in your own body: your arms and legs move on their own, your tongue speaks words in an unfamiliar language. A bell seems to toll in your head. You see everything in flashes.
The leader freezes mid-sentence in a ridiculous pose. His eyes, wide with primal terror, flash before you. His head, severed from his body, rolls across the ground.
ch.6877817a7062e46f9300666d: No, your body will never be defiled by vile magic, no spirits will touch you. You resist with every ounce of strength left. The witch’s voice whispers in your ear that you’re a fool, then fades. Right as the leader’s blade severs your head.
ch.687781bd55214a43034cb837: You smile and introduce yourself in return. The guy seems decent. Maybe later you can guide him toward the true path, to join your Order of Navigators. But that’s for later. Right now, the more pressing question is whether Mstislav can handle the witch.
ch.687781c4b618a1b138c6f8ca: You couldn’t care less about his name. What matters far more is whether he can deal with the witch. You hope he can, as does likely every living soul trapped in these swamps.
ch.687781e523ad21a5fbf4be50:
Only you and Mstislav dare to enter the hut. The corpse still lies on the floor. You shiver, though the biting cold that comes with the ghost’s presence isn’t here now.
Mstislav takes a deep breath, exhales loudly, closes his eyes, and begins reciting a prayer.
You feel a strange tremor and step back, as if making way for the words, almost a song. The candle flames in the hut flicker out, plunging everything into darkness. You hadn’t even noticed they’d been burning this whole time!
ch.687781ee3098c5ff6a93592a:
Now it’s getting cold. You hug your shoulders, shifting from foot to foot, waiting for the witch to appear, but she doesn’t. Slavka finishes the prayer, swaying slightly with his eyes closed, then sighs. The cold vanishes as abruptly as it came.
You both stand silently, listening. The hut seems to grow brighter, despite the extinguished candles.
— Well, looks like that’s it, — Mstislav says with a smile, scratching the back of his head. — No more evil here. I think we can leave now.
ch.687781f81ccbcc5602cb5443:
You step out of the hut like victors. The bandits look at you with hope. Even the leader allows himself to ask:
— That’s it? We’re free?
ch.6877820fa57acb6be31ff898: Cheers erupt. The bandits slap you and Slavka on the shoulders. The ordeal is finally over. They can finally leave.
ch.6877821dd501bb8f2de08652:
You walk away. And keep walking. And walking. It feels normal at first: maybe the distances here are just vast without magic?
But then...
ch.6877823dfdc066fea438e04d:
...you arrive back at the same hut.
It seems there’s no escape from this place.
ch.68778244871265ea10dcb70c: There’s still a chance to do things right and return the mirror to the witch!
ch.6877824f42aef7da99a5352a:
But as soon as you mention it, the leader snorts derisively.
— Hell no, I’m not giving up a damn thing.
ch.687782cdad7684ddfb627cfd: Finally, it’s over. You no longer feel the witch’s ghostly presence. You collapse to your knees, catching your breath, then quickly check your side. Nothing, just torn clothes. It seems the witch healed your wound. You whisper a silent gratitude.
ch.687782d81a97f0f7fda3ba5e:
The bandits stare at you, unsure whether to fear or praise you.
— Well, looks like the mirror’s yours now, — the young man says, snapping out of it first. You nod and try to stand.
ch.687782f2810ddd6883ad65ec:
He makes a subtle movement, and you barely dodge in time. His blade grazes your arm, cutting nearly to the bone, but better that than your heart. You can hardly hold your sword, but it’s no longer necessary.
The rebelling bandits surround their leader. You see them arguing, but only until the young man sneaks up behind him and drives a dagger under his ribs.
The leader wheezes and collapses. In a futile attempt to stay upright, he clutches at the air. No one moves to help him.
When he finally breathes his last, the young man rummages through his jacket and pulls out the mirror.
— Alright, we’ll patch you up and take the mirror to the witch! — he says with a smile.
ch.687787ad21b770c98efdbce5:
Suddenly, everyone flinches back. Some cross themselves, others curse. You jerk your head up and see the witch standing between you and the bandits.
— Vengeance, I need vengeance, — she almost growls. Her hair is disheveled, writhing like snakes. Even you feel uneasy. — They’re mine.
— But we didn’t do anything! We didn’t kill you! — someone shouts from the crowd. Everyone nods, as if that could convince a bloodthirsty otherworldly being. Is it even worth getting involved?
ch.687787f2cec442460aea3c69: This is no longer your business.
ch.6882b31e44acfd5dd15e7b11:
As soon as you speak, an icy band clamps around your throat. You clutch your neck, gasping for air.
— They killed those who killed me. They took their sins upon themselves, — the witch says without turning to you. You realize the undead have their own logic, beyond the grasp of the living. But you’re not ready to accept it! You leap to your feet and charge at the ghost, as if you could actually do something. And you believe you can, until the witch extends her hand and passes it straight through your chest.
ch.6882b3292499b80cee57f584:
At first, you feel nothing. Then your heart seems to forget how to beat. You clutch your chest and collapse.
You die to the screams and death rattles of the bandits being torn apart by the witch.
ch.6882b33e86d1a7850df26159:
You close your eyes. Maybe they didn’t kill the witch, but they burned an entire village! Perhaps this is for the best.
You keep your eyes shut until the last scream and dying gasp fade. When it’s over, the witch is beside you.
— Bring me the mirror!
ch.688b66caafc1aba624722439:
The leader turns to you, glaring with contempt.
— And if have it, so what? You gonna take it from me? Think you're up for it?
ch.688b67ad75e02713bc02e77e:
Suddenly, everyone flinches back. Some cross themselves, others curse. You jerk your head up and see the witch standing between you and the bandits.
— Vengeance, I need vengeance, — she almost growls. Her hair is disheveled, writhing like snakes. Even you feel uneasy. — They’re mine.
— But we didn’t do anything! We didn’t kill you! — someone shouts from the crowd. Everyone nods, as if that could convince a bloodthirsty otherworldly being. Is it even worth getting involved?
ch.6899c0f38dd72da50ae7242d:
She touches you, and a chill spreads from the contact through your body. Your wounds close, breathing becomes easier, and the pain fades.
— Find the mirror.
It’s clear the witch didn’t do this out of kindness, she wants you to fulfill her demand quickly.
ch.6899c1e5ddb734a7304022f5:
You close your eyes. Maybe they didn’t kill the witch, but they burned an entire village! Perhaps this is for the best.
You keep your eyes shut until the last scream and dying gasp fade. When it’s over, the witch is beside you.
— Bring me the mirror!

You keep your eyes shut until the last scream and dying gasp fade. When it’s over, the witch is beside you.

— Find the mirror.

You keep your eyes shut until the last scream and dying gasp fade. When it’s over, the witch is beside you.
— Bring me the mirror!
ch.689c6d794fe50ff9942b2d21: Try to gain their trust. With sausage.
ch.689c6dcf48c70c8d466a2fe3:
You need to talk to these people to find the artifact for the witch.
And what brings people closer than food?
You pull a piece of sausage bought in the village from your pack and approach the men.
ch.689c6ddbd2b0b1ead301aaac: "I’ve got food. I’ll give it to you if you tell me something."
ch.689c6de37a72829bdcefc20c: "Hey! Want to eat? Answer my questions first!"
ch.689c6e1303ba5b6f39a5b3d5:
The men freeze in surprise, staring at you wide-eyed. Their gazes drop to the sausage in your hands. Hunger flares in their eyes instantly.

— Who the hell are you? And why so bold? — the shrill-voiced one sneers, drawing his sword.
ch.689c6e958bcad34c0010e733: "Don’t play dumb, I heard everything. You won’t find any more supplies here."
ch.689c6ed4279990335031bc08:
You decide to press the bandits, but you misjudge how desperate they are.

— You can show off somewhere else, — the shrill one advances on you. The second, with an accent, snorts and adds:

— On the other side.

Both lunge at you, swords bared.
ch.689c6edd7fef3c34d45c32be:
— Hold it right there, — the accented one also draws his sword. You step back, not taking your eyes off them. They’re fixated on the sausage in your hands.

It happens too fast, you don’t even have time to draw the sword the witch gave you. Both men charge like starving dogs, teeth bared, movements jerky. They know exactly what they’re doing.
ch.689c6f3b0e489eaadc7c3a9c:
You make a desperate attempt to flee. To hell with the burned village, the witch, and her request! You just want to live.

But it’s no use. The men, though hungry, are clearly better trained than you. One catches up.
ch.689c6f4a563d4717728d273e:
You know it’s the end. You can’t outrun these bandits: hungry or not, they’re faster, better trained.

You don’t even feel the pain as the shrill one’s blade severs your head in one swing. Your body collapses, fingers clutching the sausage in a death spasm. The bandits pry it from your grip, but you no longer care.

You’re dead.
ch.689c6f7602d41260df62a293:
A sharp pain. Your legs give out: your spine severed by a sword. You choke on terror, glancing down to see the blade’s tip protruding near your solar plexus.

You fall to your knees, then face-first. The sausage slips from your hands. One bandit steps closer and takes it. The other argues with him, but you can’t make out the words. Consciousness fades.

You die.

cz.68776e51a583a513398d76fe:
— My murderers must face punishment. But first, you must return what they stole from me.
You don’t know how to respond. It’s like everything’s already been decided for you. But maybe you should try something...
cz.68776f130a3d5213d0b5b8aa:
The ghost leans forward, stopping mere inches from your face. Her voice turns into an eerie, otherworldly hiss.
— I don’t care. You’re here, so you’ll manage, — she says, pulling back with a careless shrug. — You don’t need to be a warrior. Being a thief will do.
cz.68776f27279785c6efb5aa5f:
— They came from the village by the road. Their home is there, and so is my stolen mirror. Bring it back to me.
You nod resignedly. The ghost glides beside you, placing her hand on your cheek. Or she would have, if she were alive. Instead, you feel an unbearable cold. Your cheek goes numb, but you stand still, unmoving. The witch pulls away and gestures toward the sword protruding from her body.
— Take this sword. You might need it. Now go, and don’t fail me.
cz.68776f9e898fc18e5b451dc3:
You step out of the hut and exhale shakily. A gentle breeze warms your chilled body. Rubbing your cheeks with your hands, you shrug off the lingering cold and adjust the bag on your shoulder. Now, a sword rests inside it.
You still haven’t fully processed what happened. Did you ever think you’d meet a ghost? Or help one?
But you have no choice. The witch’s magic won’t let you leave the swamps. You must do as she asked.
cz.68776fb1e03472f2f9d57bd9:
You head toward the village. This time, you don’t wander and walk straight to it.
At first, you don’t realize what’s wrong, but then the sparse swamp trees part, revealing the full scene.
The village is burned and pillaged. You freeze in place.
cz.68776fc7ac55d85e4e94c8a2: The wind carries the suffocating stench of smoke and burned flesh. You see corpses, such devastation... You want to flee, but your task holds you here. You must reach Targrad, no matter the cost. Perhaps the witch’s murderers are already dead... If so, bringing her the artifact might be enough. You hope it will satisfy her.
cz.68776fcafea5ef3f947f96d0:
The witch said her murderers were holed up in this village. But what do you do if they’re all dead now? Will the ghost listen to you? Or will she think you’re trying to deceive her?  
You realize you’re in deep trouble. But maybe you can at least find the artifact?
cz.68776fe61d62f818144929b3:
You approach the edge of the ruined village, crouching and moving cautiously. Whoever destroyed this place couldn’t have gotten far. The witch’s curse wouldn’t allow it.
Suddenly, you hear voices. They’re not begging for help or mourning the dead; they’re discussing mundane things. You realize these are the ones who attacked the village.
cz.687770119a6b54bdde1a5e09: Well, you’ve got nothing to lose. If they’re trapped here like you, maybe they won’t attack right away. If they do, death might spare you from carrying out the witch’s errand.
cz.6877701680ac1c8fc0a67cf8:
You decide to stay hidden for now. Who knows what these men, capable of destroying an entire village, might do to you? Luckily, none of them notice you.
You press yourself against the corner of a burned-out house and listen.
One man has a deep voice with a slight, unfamiliar accent. The other speaks without an accent, his voice higher and almost shrill.
— How can a village like this have so few supplies? I’m starving, and there’s nothing, — grumbles the one with the accent.
— We’re gonna die here! These swamps are cursed, and we’ve got no idea how to break the spell, — the shrill one replies hysterically. You realize they’re trapped here by the curse too. And they’re hungry.
cz.687770255d653efcf402554c:
You step forward, raising your hands to show you come in peace. Several tired-looking men stand before you. They grip their weapons tighter, eyeing you with wary fear as you emerge from behind the half-burned house.
— A live one, — says one of the men, slightly relaxing his shoulders. — Who are you?
You hear a faint accent in his voice, but you can’t place it. Not that it matters right now.
cz.68777038f3c351577685307e:
— I swear, chief knows something. Like, why we’re stuck here, — the shrill one lowers his voice, forcing you to lean forward to hear.
— Cut it out. How would he know? — The one with the accent seems less suspicious. — Don’t badmouth our leader!
— Alright, alright, it's just a theory!
You hear their footsteps fade as the men walk away.
cz.68777068417fdab26ffb8723:
You think the men might reveal more useful information. You follow them as quietly as possible, straining to listen, but you get too caught up and step on a dry, heat-cracked branch. It snaps loudly, and the men hear it.
— Who’s there? Come out now!
cz.687770798620a3432a97173b: Step out from your hiding spot.
cz.68777097aef5de13e6265bc8:
You can’t think of anything better than to bolt. You dart around the corner. The house you were hiding behind is missing a wall, so the men spot you.
— Stop, you little rat! — the shrill one yells. You notice him giving chase. The other man, for some reason, is nowhere in sight.
cz.687770ab8a0d6fb48d25b5cb: But not for long. He suddenly appears in front of you, stepping out from around a corner. You veer to the side, but there’s a pile of half-burned logs blocking your path. Behind you, the shrill one is closing in. You’re trapped.
cz.687770bdc888ca05f005a144: "I’m a messenger of the Order of Navigators!"
cz.687770c4d13a96e750824979:
— Then why were you eavesdropping? — the one with the accent asks, still skeptical, though he lowers his sword.
— Yeah, and why’d you run? — the shrill one chimes in.
cz.687770c82e35b771f834f773: — We’ve never heard of that, — the accented one says, drawing his sword again and eyeing you suspiciously. You’ve got one last card to play.
cz.6877710b743696531c94767d:
The men exchange glances and burst into synchronized laughter.
— What’s so funny? — a new voice booms, low and harsh. Both men snap to attention. You turn around.
From behind the ruins of another burned house, several more figures emerge. They’re clearly from the same band: exhausted, angry, and deeply terrified beneath it all.
— Who’s this now? — a tall man in leather armor stares at you. His mustache is sharply twisted, and his gaze drips with disdain and distrust.
Well, it seems this is the leader. You’re already exhausted from dealing with bandits today!
cz.68777142b10562bdb441afbc: "I’m just a messenger of the Order of Navigators."
cz.687771498198fb94b7c7f178:
The men exchange glances at your words.
— Never heard of it. Where’d you come from? All the locals are long dead.
They tense up again and start closing in on you.
cz.6877714dcd7817d80cab402c:
Now the men look at you differently.
— We’ve been trying to get out of here for who knows how long! — says one who’d been silent until now. The other elbows him in the side.
— Just spill everything already!
— What’s it matter? Maybe he’s been sent to sort this mess and get us out!
cz.68777164c6503bbfbef44368: "I know something... Maybe I can help."
cz.68777172ecaff18af8343399:
You realize this is your chance, there won’t be another. The men stare at you, as if weighing your words. Something you said clearly struck a chord.
Suddenly, there’s a noise nearby. From behind the ruins of another burned house, several more figures emerge. They’re clearly part of the same band: exhausted, angry, and deeply terrified beneath it all.
— Who’s this now? — a tall man in leather armor stares at you. His mustache is sharply twisted, and his gaze drips with disdain and distrust. Your new acquaintances both snap to attention.
Well, it seems this is the leader. You’re already exhausted from dealing with bandits today!
cz.6877717c1c47f3efb21336d5:
— He says he’s trapped here like us. Says he might help, — one of them introduces you. The leader squints and sneers.
— And how’s this runt supposed to help us? Can you even hold a sword?
cz.687771b646f9b37bd9a181fb: "I know what will get us all out of here."
cz.687771bd405ba3f4e15b922c:
The bandit leader raises an eyebrow, then laughs with a cruel, mocking sound. His lackeys join in, their laughter hollow.
— In what, then? Writing? We don’t need scribes. Words? Those are useless too.
cz.687771c1612fd19c7a89c97d: "I know what will get us all out of here."
cz.687771cda360c1de351bf14a:
You see the entire group staring at you, hope flickering in their eyes. The leader, though, isn’t convinced.
— Why should we trust you? Tell us what you know first, then we’ll decide if you’re worth believing.
cz.687771f65c6bc4cd5a76e726:
You decide there’s no point in hiding anything. These bandits want to escape the cursed swamps just as badly as you do. Right now, you’re allies, and many of them likely understand that.
— It’s all because of the locals. They killed the swamp witch and stole a valuable artifact. She wants it back. And, of course, she wants revenge.
A few bandits glance around nervously, as if looking for those responsible for the witch’s death. But alas, they’re the ones who killed them.
cz.687771fb4af817d6da36adb1:
These are the bandits who wiped out an entire village. Trusting them completely would be foolish. What if they kill you as soon as they hear the truth? You decide to play it safe.
— t’s because of the witch. She was killed and robbed by the people of this village. She sent me to find what was stolen. If anything happens to me, she’ll destroy everyone in the area.
Of course, the witch never said you were particularly important, but the bandits don’t need to know that.
You see in their eyes that they believe you. Now they look at you with more respect than before. Some even step back slightly, as if afraid.
cz.68777209d2f6c5d9902e84b5: — So, what do you suggest we do? — the leader asks, frowning and staring at you expectantly.
cz.6877724575c61507df6aa339: "We need to find the stolen mirror."
cz.68777248a82ae5340e85a3b4: "We need to figure out how to trick the witch."
cz.6877725b6e4d07907a24ec43:
Why come up with something new when the witch already gave you a clear path? Sure, you can’t punish the guilty, but maybe that’s for the best?
The bandit leader frowns discontentedly. Something shifts in his movements, but you can’t quite place what. You’re distracted by the high-pitched voice of a young man standing just behind him.  
— We did see a strange mirror that doesn’t burn! A round one.
The leader spins toward the young man and practically growls:
— That’s definitely. Not. It!
You freeze, as does the young man. That kind of reaction can only mean one thing.
cz.6877725ec0232b786f36d303:
You realize the witch probably won’t be satisfied with just the artifact. And that’s not even considering how you’ll get it in the first place. You start to think, but the same young man who mentioned the mirror suddenly speaks up again.
— What if we just banish the witch? — everyone turns to look at him, and he shrugs, — I would’ve tried earlier, but we didn’t know about the witch!
cz.68777ec7e80e2cdbbbf16d59: "Do you know how to do that?"
cz.68777ecb09285caee7e293ed: "Is there anyone here who knows how to do that?"
cz.68777eea8cf0f973aecd50a8:
— Well, yeah, I know how, — the young man says, puffing out his chest with a boastful grin. — I was a priest with Turva’s band. I’ve done crazier things than this!
It’s a reasonable idea. But can you really trust your life to some young kid?
cz.68777eed0334393e733d8657:
— Yeah, I do, — the young man says, spreading his arms, — I was a priest with Turva’s band. I’ve done crazier things than this.
It’s a solid idea. But can you really trust your life to some kid?
cz.68777f1371ec3fda827cd7a4: You shake your head. Maybe the kid really is a priest, but taking such a risk... You want to escape these swamps, not get stuck here forever because of an angry witch’s whim.
cz.68777f1a90768808625407d6:
Here goes nothing! You agree to the young man’s plan. The leader rubs his chin thoughtfully, then shrugs:
— Might as well try. We’ve got nothing to lose.
He turns his gaze to you.
— Alright, lead the way to where this witch of yours is hiding.
cz.68777f632cb5f630737f0645: "We need to find the stolen mirror."
cz.68777fdde9dbf46430a8b89a:
You lead the group through the swamps, heading straight for the hut. The journey seems to take longer than it should, but you brush off the strangeness.
You stop right in front of the hut. The young man who claims to be a priest tugs at your sleeve to get your attention.
— By the way, I’m Mstislav. Call me Slavka, — he says with a grin, nodding toward the hut. — Just thought you should know the name of the guy who’s gonna banish that witch, right?
He laughs, as if he’s not scared at all.
cz.68777ff59f3cf8c68c46e6a3:
The leader turns to you, glaring with disdain.
— And if I’ve got the mirror, so what? You gonna take it from me? Think you're up for it?
cz.68778003999b2330c41b3ccb:
Your body aches from what happened just hours ago. You draw your sword, but your movements are clumsy. The bandit leader smirks, watching your struggle with the weapon.
— You’ve never held anything heavier than a quill, you little punk!
He deftly draws his own sword and advances, winding up for a strike. You realize the force of his blow will be too much for you to block.
cz.6877800552157c87b8a740c7:
You surprisingly draw your sword with ease. Traces of the witch’s blood still stain the blade, but you pay it no mind. You have a goal, and nothing stands in your way. You grip the hilt tightly and lock eyes with the leader.
— Look at this serious guy! — they mock, but you don’t take the bait.
The leader draws his weapon and comes at you, winding up for a strike.
cz.6877809c1f2529646b28b4de:
You slide to the side, dodging the path of the strike. The sword whistles past your ear but doesn’t touch you. The leader spins with the momentum, trying to hit you again. You leap back.
The other bandits haven’t joined the fight yet. You see confusion on their faces. It’s dawning on them that their leader is willing to sacrifice both his life and theirs for greed.
You realize you could call out to them. But doing so might distract you, leaving you open to the leader’s next strike.
cz.6877809f9322bd17f049d9e6: ...But what does it matter? The fury of battle engulfs you, its fire burning hot. You meet the leader’s strike with your blade... or try to, as the force of his blow obliterates your barely prepared defense. You’re knocked to the side, tripping over a charred piece of wood and falling. You don’t scream, no, just curse and struggle to get up.
cz.687780e458982e675f3b55ec:
The leader steps closer and spits near you. For a moment, you freeze, looking up at him.
— Too much pride, you little punk, — he sneers, raising his sword above you, — Send my regards to that witch of yours.
He swings down. The blade cuts through your unarmored body like butter, slicing your heart.
You die before you can take your final breath.
cz.687780f9863b6ec75207f1a5: "Don’t you see he’s ready to risk your lives for his own gain?!"
cz.68778108bc8407c6acdf1e18:
You notice a few bandits flinch, exchanging glances. You know standing up alone against someone stronger is always terrifying, but there are so many of them! You hope for their common sense.  
And you’re not wrong.
The young man who mentioned the mirror is the first to raise his hand.
— He’s really ready to cling to that mirror until he dies!
Another man nods, grabbing his battle axe.
— Yeah, until we all die here like dogs! How many days have we been slogging through these swamps?! My junk’s already crawling with leeches!
One by one, they start grumbling angrily. You’d love to listen, but the leader clearly plans to deal with you first before sorting out the others.
cz.6877810c4dcbc02930d301bc:
There’s no time to get distracted. Dying a martyr to some pathetic deserter bandit’s blade isn’t the fate you dreamed of.

You miss the chance to gain allies but don’t miss the leader’s strike. Dodging just in time, you swing back, but he deftly parries and nicks you with his sword. The blade tears through your clothes and slices your side. You scream in pain.

— Not so brave now, huh? — the leader taunts, stepping closer. His eyes gleam with bloodlust.

Suddenly, you feel a presence, something intangible to ordinary senses. The air grows colder, and you shiver. Something is trying to merge with you. You hear a faint whisper: "Let me in".
cz.68778175a6d0eaf0f969dd89:
You’ve felt this cold before, back in the swamp hut. The witch has come to your aid, and who are you to refuse her?
You let her in, gasping from the icy chill. It feels like being plunged into a frozen lake in winter.
From that moment, you’re a passenger in your own body: your arms and legs move on their own, your tongue speaks words in an unfamiliar language. A bell seems to toll in your head. You see everything in flashes.
The leader freezes mid-sentence in a ridiculous pose. His eyes, wide with primal terror, flash before you. His head, severed from his body, rolls across the ground.
cz.6877817a7062e46f9300666d: No, your body will never be defiled by vile magic, no spirits will touch you. You resist with every ounce of strength left. The witch’s voice whispers in your ear that you’re a fool, then fades. Right as the leader’s blade severs your head.
cz.687781bd55214a43034cb837: You smile and introduce yourself in return. The guy seems decent. Maybe later you can guide him toward the true path, to join your Order of Navigators. But that’s for later. Right now, the more pressing question is whether Mstislav can handle the witch.
cz.687781c4b618a1b138c6f8ca: You couldn’t care less about his name. What matters far more is whether he can deal with the witch. You hope he can, as does likely every living soul trapped in these swamps.
cz.687781e523ad21a5fbf4be50:
Only you and Mstislav dare to enter the hut. The corpse still lies on the floor. You shiver, though the biting cold that comes with the ghost’s presence isn’t here now.
Mstislav takes a deep breath, exhales loudly, closes his eyes, and begins reciting a prayer.
You feel a strange tremor and step back, as if making way for the words, almost a song. The candle flames in the hut flicker out, plunging everything into darkness. You hadn’t even noticed they’d been burning this whole time!
cz.687781ee3098c5ff6a93592a:
Now it’s getting cold. You hug your shoulders, shifting from foot to foot, waiting for the witch to appear, but she doesn’t. Slavka finishes the prayer, swaying slightly with his eyes closed, then sighs. The cold vanishes as abruptly as it came.
You both stand silently, listening. The hut seems to grow brighter, despite the extinguished candles.
— Well, looks like that’s it, — Mstislav says with a smile, scratching the back of his head. — No more evil here. I think we can leave now.
cz.687781f81ccbcc5602cb5443:
You step out of the hut like victors. The bandits look at you with hope. Even the leader allows himself to ask:
— That’s it? We’re free?
cz.6877820fa57acb6be31ff898: Cheers erupt. The bandits slap you and Slavka on the shoulders. The ordeal is finally over. They can finally leave.
cz.6877821dd501bb8f2de08652:
You walk away. And keep walking. And walking. It feels normal at first: maybe the distances here are just vast without magic?
But then...
cz.6877823dfdc066fea438e04d:
...you arrive back at the same hut.
It seems there’s no escape from this place.
cz.68778244871265ea10dcb70c: There’s still a chance to do things right and return the mirror to the witch!
cz.6877824f42aef7da99a5352a:
But as soon as you mention it, the leader snorts derisively.
— Hell no, I’m not giving up a damn thing.
cz.687782cdad7684ddfb627cfd: Finally, it’s over. You no longer feel the witch’s ghostly presence. You collapse to your knees, catching your breath, then quickly check your side. Nothing, just torn clothes. It seems the witch healed your wound. You whisper a silent gratitude.
cz.687782d81a97f0f7fda3ba5e:
The bandits stare at you, unsure whether to fear or praise you.
— Well, looks like the mirror’s yours now, — the young man says, snapping out of it first. You nod and try to stand.
cz.687782f2810ddd6883ad65ec:
He makes a subtle movement, and you barely dodge in time. His blade grazes your arm, cutting nearly to the bone, but better that than your heart. You can hardly hold your sword, but it’s no longer necessary.
The rebelling bandits surround their leader. You see them arguing, but only until the young man sneaks up behind him and drives a dagger under his ribs.
The leader wheezes and collapses. In a futile attempt to stay upright, he clutches at the air. No one moves to help him.
When he finally breathes his last, the young man rummages through his jacket and pulls out the mirror.
— Alright, we’ll patch you up and take the mirror to the witch! — he says with a smile.
cz.687787ad21b770c98efdbce5:
Suddenly, everyone flinches back. Some cross themselves, others curse. You jerk your head up and see the witch standing between you and the bandits.
— Vengeance, I need vengeance, — she almost growls. Her hair is disheveled, writhing like snakes. Even you feel uneasy. — They’re mine.
— But we didn’t do anything! We didn’t kill you! — someone shouts from the crowd. Everyone nods, as if that could convince a bloodthirsty otherworldly being. Is it even worth getting involved?
cz.687787f2cec442460aea3c69: This is no longer your business.
cz.6882b31e44acfd5dd15e7b11:
As soon as you speak, an icy band clamps around your throat. You clutch your neck, gasping for air.
— They killed those who killed me. They took their sins upon themselves, — the witch says without turning to you. You realize the undead have their own logic, beyond the grasp of the living. But you’re not ready to accept it! You leap to your feet and charge at the ghost, as if you could actually do something. And you believe you can, until the witch extends her hand and passes it straight through your chest.
cz.6882b3292499b80cee57f584:
At first, you feel nothing. Then your heart seems to forget how to beat. You clutch your chest and collapse.
You die to the screams and death rattles of the bandits being torn apart by the witch.
cz.6882b33e86d1a7850df26159:
You close your eyes. Maybe they didn’t kill the witch, but they burned an entire village! Perhaps this is for the best.
You keep your eyes shut until the last scream and dying gasp fade. When it’s over, the witch is beside you.
— Bring me the mirror!
cz.688b66caafc1aba624722439:
The leader turns to you, glaring with contempt.
— And if have it, so what? You gonna take it from me? Think you're up for it?
cz.688b67ad75e02713bc02e77e:
Suddenly, everyone flinches back. Some cross themselves, others curse. You jerk your head up and see the witch standing between you and the bandits.
— Vengeance, I need vengeance, — she almost growls. Her hair is disheveled, writhing like snakes. Even you feel uneasy. — They’re mine.
— But we didn’t do anything! We didn’t kill you! — someone shouts from the crowd. Everyone nods, as if that could convince a bloodthirsty otherworldly being. Is it even worth getting involved?
cz.6899c0f38dd72da50ae7242d:
She touches you, and a chill spreads from the contact through your body. Your wounds close, breathing becomes easier, and the pain fades.
— Find the mirror.
It’s clear the witch didn’t do this out of kindness, she wants you to fulfill her demand quickly.
